name: Leslie "Wildfire" Hernandez
caption: A young member of the Furies trained by Vyolynce and Tigress, dropped in her first singles outing to LEW's final Women's Champion.

tenures.note: Billed from Cape Fear, North Carolina, accompanied by Angel; lost a non-title singles match to Sierra Browne. Teamed with Tigress and Angel as the Coven on 22 October 2003, pinning Leanna Love with a top-rope Santa Maria in a win over the Love Sisters and Comedy. Teamed with Angel as the Furies in a losing effort by disqualification against the Bod Squad (Bliss, Tara "Sunburst" Marshall) on 12 November 2003, refusing to release a leg-and-hair stretch on Bliss through the ropes. Lost to Donna Tetreault by referee stoppage on 24 March 2004 after being knocked out with a ringside bucket, now accompanied by Ravnos Romani rather than Angel. Lost to "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict by pinfall on 5 May 2004 despite twice nearly winning by small package; Benedict applied a post-match Morbid Sting until Arielle Starr ran in to break it up. Joked with the Amazing Romanis backstage about a soda can before their own tag win on 25 May 2005, then clashed in the locker room with newcomer Amazing Grace over the state of the women's division. Ran in to save Lisa Drake from a Bod Squad beatdown on 8 June 2005 after John DeWolfe's own dismissal of the women's division, then fought a tense backstage encounter with newcomer Amazing Grace before teaming with Drake against Alicia Powers and "Tornado" Tara Smith in a match the Bod Squad broke up as a no contest. Ran down to help clear the ring of the Bod Squad during the Wind Walkers' own women's tag match on 20 July 2005, throwing Amazing Grace from the ring with a headscissors. Made the save for Arielle Starr against Amazing Grace and Kari Stevens on 3 August 2005, agreeing to team with Starr against the pair at Gold Rush. Teamed with Ravnos Romani in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, pinning Alicia Powers with a bridging German suplex before "Tornado" Tara Smith eliminated her.

name: Paul Wong
caption: One of the tag team the Machines and the reigning UWF Rampage Champion, retaining his title by disqualification against Tom Landis after Team Canada interfered.

tenures.note: Billed from Denver, Colorado, weighing 276 pounds; entered as the reigning UWF Rampage Champion. Retained the title by disqualification over Tom Landis, then was beaten down by Team Canada until Alex Kidd made the save. Retained again on 30 August 2003, pinning Cameron Black with a tilt-a-whirl powerslam after Serge Annis's appearance froze Black in place. Lost the UWF Rampage Championship to the One-Winged Angel by pinfall on 4 October 2003. Teamed with Alex Kidd, Youth Gone Wild, and Quinn Brown to a count-out win over the Pride on 22 October 2003, turning manager Kari Stevens's own pepper spray back on Tom Landis. Lost to Scott Daniels by pinfall on 15 November 2003 after a low blow and Daniels using the ropes for leverage. Entered the 17 December 2003 Meltdown Championship tournament as the reigning UWF Rampage Champion's own former MBC rival, eliminated last from the battle royal by Victor Frost; beat Tigress in the semi-finals with a Samoan drop, then lost the finals to Papa Legba, pinned by the Black Magic superbomb. Teamed with Alex Kidd and "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee against Team Canada and Scott Daniels on 15 May 2004 in a six-man tag that ended without a decision amid a mass brawl; Serge Annis and Caliban ambushed and hospitalized him in his own locker room after the match. Beat "Dark Horse" Randall Osbourne by pinfall with a lariat on 8 September 2004, then lost the tournament semifinal to Vyolynce by disqualification after Brian McKenzie's run-in. Returned from a concussion to team with Sierra Browne against Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie on 11 December 2004, nearly finishing McKenzie with a gorilla press before Tetreault knocked him out with smuggled brass knuckles for the loss. Took a call from a nephew stuck at boarding school on 8 June 2005, unable to reach the boy's own father, Simon O'Neal. Rescued Stephanie Harper from a backstage assault by Brian McKenzie on 3 August 2005; lost the Brawl From The Mall 6 opener to the Mercenary by pinfall on 6 August 2005, then was ambushed backstage by McKenzie and Donna Tetreault with a steel chair and brass knuckles. Brawled with Chris O'Brien at ringside throughout Donna Tetreault's own No Disqualification match with Simon O'Neal on 18 March 2006. Reflected in a backstage conversation with Stephanie Harper on 7 June 2006 on his own long rivalry with the Fraternity Boys, recalling his own past powerbomb on Gus Zampitella and worrying aloud about how far the feud with Brian McKenzie and Chris O'Brien would go; did not wrestle.

name: Cameron Black
caption: A trenchcoated brawler of Sabbat Justice whose singles match against Papa Legba was ruled a no-contest after he fled the ring during Serge Annis's interference.

tenures.note: Billed from Anchorage, Alaska, weighing 275 pounds. Fled the ring against Papa Legba once Serge Annis interfered on 9 August 2003; the match was never decided. Lost the UWF Rampage Championship match to champion Paul Wong by pinfall on 30 August 2003 after Serge Annis's appearance froze him in place. On 24 September 2003, his singles match against Tom Landis was thrown out as a no-contest when Serge Annis and the Pride brawled; agreed afterward to face Annis one-on-one two weeks later in Las Vegas. Entered the 17 December 2003 battle royal but voluntarily left through the crowd rather than continue after eliminating Avanter, his mind still on Serge Annis. On 20 December 2003, Serge Annis ambushed him with a lead pipe before his own scheduled match; Black still knocked out opponent Collision Holly with a single right hand for the win, then assaulted Vice-President Jessica Marshall in her office, forcing her to book a Barbed Wire Match against Annis at Eve of Destruction.

name: "Deadly" Derek Irvin
caption: A bandaged singles competitor billed "Bonebreaker," pinned by Tragedy in a hard-fought non-title match after nearly forcing a submission win of his own.

tenures.note: Nearly won by crossface submission before Tragedy reached the ropes on 9 August 2003; lost by pinfall to Tragedy's Sleepy Hollow Driver. Teamed with Avanter and the Arcana's opponents, Tragedy and Eugene Robinson, in a six-man tag on 4 October 2003, disqualified after striking his own partner Tragedy with a steel chair amid a locker-room prank by the Sons of Cacaphony and Alex Extreme.

name: "Banshee" Michael Keening
caption: One half of the Ghost Dancers, the reigning UWF World Tag Team Champions, who retained by default when their three-way title defense was thrown out as a no-contest.

tenures.note: Billed with his brother Jason Keening as the Ghost Dancers, descendants of the Paiute nation from Los Angeles; also confronted Serge Annis over an old injury to their brother-in-law Gabriel Whitecross. Lost the UWF World Tag Team Championship with his brother to Team Canada on 4 October 2003 after Kari Stevens pepper-sprayed Jason Keening at ringside; the Privateers ambushed both brothers backstage afterward. Sabotaged the Privateers' cricket bats in a woodchipper before winning the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with his brother from Team Canada by submission on 25 October 2003, after a contract clause kept the World Tag Team Championship off the line. Lost the UWF North American Tag Team Championship on 15 November 2003 when teammates Erik and Chad Grimsson escaped the Tower of Doom cage as a complete team first; he and his brother Jason escaped afterward. Entered the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match with brother Jason; pinned Jacob Drake with a Gourdbuster before eventually being pinned himself by Drake's own Gourdbuster in return. Teamed with brother Jason and Erik Grimsson in a six-man tag loss to Team Canada and Scott Daniels on 10 March 2004 after two unidentified men in suits ambushed the match; Daniels stole the pinfall off him. Beat "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker by pinfall on 21 March 2004 with a top-rope somersault splash, following an old backstage confrontation with Alex Extreme over Extreme's own alliance with Michael Augustine. Teamed with Erik Grimsson in a scrambled-partners tag on 5 May 2004 against a reluctant pairing of Niklos Romani and Todd Franklin; the bout ended as a no-contest after Franklin turned on his own partner and battered all three other wrestlers. Teamed with brother Jason again as the Ghost Dancers on 29 May 2004, fighting Serge Annis and Caliban to a double countout after a suicida dive and other big moves at ringside; the Privateers ran in on the ensuing brawl, and commissioner Becky Byers added the Ghost Dancers to the Gold Rush UWF World Tag Team Championship match against champions the Privateers and Annis and Caliban. Teamed with brother Jason as the Ghost Dancers in a losing Gold Rush triple threat for the UWF World Tag Team Championship on 5 June 2004, pinned by Jacob Drake of the champion Privateers after a Near Death Experience-style superplex from Serge Annis left him unable to continue; collapsed backstage afterward with a back injury and was taken to a hospital.

name: "The Hammer" Trevor Hextall
caption: One half of Team Canada and one of the UWF North American Tag Team Champions, whose interference cost Tom Landis a title match before the pair joined the main event's three-way brawl.

tenures.note: Billed with Bob Jablonski as Team Canada and the reigning UWF North American Tag Team Champions. Interfered in the Rampage Championship match, then competed in the main event three-way, ruled a no-contest, on 9 August 2003. Pinned Jason Keening with a double heartpunch on 4 October 2003 to win the UWF World Tag Team Championship, adding it to the team's own North American Tag Team title. Teamed with the Pride in a non-title, count-out loss on 22 October 2003. Submitted to the Ghost Dancers' stereo scorpion deathlocks on 25 October 2003, losing the UWF North American Tag Team Championship after a fine-print contract clause kept the team's own World Tag Team Championship off the line. Teamed with Jablonski to retain the UWF World Tag Team Championship over Eugene Robinson and Youth Gone Wild on 12 November 2003. Entered the Tower of Doom on 15 November 2003 alongside the Privateers, keeping Chad Grimsson from escaping the cage for several minutes before the Sons of Cacaphony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) escaped first and took the UWF North American Tag Team Championship. Entered the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match with Bob Jablonski as Team Canada; pinned by Chad Grimsson's Rib Wrecker combination for the elimination. Teamed with Bob Jablonski and Scott Daniels on 10 March 2004 in a six-man tag win over the Ghost Dancers and Erik Grimsson, Daniels stealing the pinfall on Michael Keening after two unidentified men in suits ambushed the Ghost Dancers' side. Teamed with Bob Jablonski and Scott Daniels again against Alex Kidd, Paul Wong, and "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee on 15 May 2004 in a six-man tag that ended without a decision amid a mass brawl. Teamed with Bob Jablonski as Team Canada again on 29 May 2004, ambushing debuting Alex Martinez in the aisle with Tom Landis and Kari Stevens before the bell, then legdropping a would-be saving Alex Extreme to protect Jablonski's pinfall over the exhausted Martinez. Teamed with Bob Jablonski as Team Canada in a Gold Rush loss to Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian) on 5 June 2004, pinned after a top-rope Frog Splash. Teamed with Bob Jablonski and Tom Landis in a Meltdown main event win over Quinn Brown and Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian) on 25 August 2004, Landis and Hextall's own Game Misconduct heart-punch combination flooring Andrew Tucker for the pin. Teamed with Bob Jablonski and manager-turned-competitor Kari Stevens in a losing intergender six-way against Fury (Rage, Spice) and Ami Tran by pinfall on 6 October 2004, Tran finishing Stevens with a version of the One-Winged Angel's own Revelator. Teamed with Bob Jablonski as Team Canada in a no-contest against the Hands of Death (Caliban, Serge Annis) on 13 November 2004, clipping Caliban's knee with a hockey stick before the bout dissolved into a mass brawl. Teamed with Bob Jablonski and Scott Daniels as the Pride, beating Amity (the One-Winged Angel, Rage, Spice) in the Bluff City Streetfight main event on 27 November 2004 after Derek Martin turned on the One-Winged Angel to score the pinfall. Beat "Hentai" Ryu Osawa by pinfall (a heart punch, with manager Kari Stevens tying Osawa in the ropes) on 1 December 2004, then joined Bob Jablonski in a beatdown of the fallen Osawa broken up by a returning "Showtime" Rick Marley. On 11 December 2004, brawled with Rage backstage in a Pride-Fury melee, grabbing a lead pipe before Ryu Osawa intervened and was jumped for it. Was part of the Pride's own ringside entrance and locker-room scenes on 28 May 2005, celebrating the group's Rise to Power sweep and welcoming the returning Brett Greene alongside the rest of the group.

name: "Bonebreaker" Bob Jablonski
caption: One half of Team Canada and one of the UWF North American Tag Team Champions, whose interference cost Tom Landis a title match before the pair joined the main event's three-way brawl.

tenures.note: Billed with Trevor Hextall as Team Canada and the reigning UWF North American Tag Team Champions. Interfered in the Rampage Championship match, then competed in the main event three-way, ruled a no-contest, on 9 August 2003. Teamed with Hextall to pin Jason Keening on 4 October 2003, winning the UWF World Tag Team Championship to add to the team's own North American Tag Team title. Teamed with the Pride in a non-title, count-out loss on 22 October 2003. Lost the UWF North American Tag Team Championship to the Ghost Dancers by submission on 25 October 2003, after a fine-print contract clause kept the team's own World Tag Team Championship off the line. Teamed with Hextall to retain the UWF World Tag Team Championship over Eugene Robinson and Youth Gone Wild on 12 November 2003. Entered the Tower of Doom on 15 November 2003 alongside the Privateers, on the losing side as the Sons of Cacaphony became the first complete team to escape and won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship. Entered the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match with Trevor Hextall as Team Canada; pinned Erik Grimsson after manager Kari Stevens cracked him with a hockey stick, then was pinned himself by Edmond Winston IV's Cobra Clutch suplex, which stole the fall from Winston's own teammate Chad Grimsson. Teamed with Trevor Hextall and Scott Daniels on 10 March 2004 in a six-man tag win over the Ghost Dancers and Erik Grimsson, Daniels stealing the pinfall on Michael Keening after two unidentified men in suits ambushed the Ghost Dancers' side. Teamed with Trevor Hextall and Scott Daniels again against Alex Kidd, Paul Wong, and "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee on 15 May 2004 in a six-man tag that ended without a decision amid a mass brawl. Teamed with Trevor Hextall as Team Canada again on 29 May 2004, ambushing debuting Alex Martinez in the aisle with Tom Landis and Kari Stevens before the bell, then pinning the exhausted Martinez, who never tagged into the match, for the win. Teamed with Trevor Hextall as Team Canada in a Gold Rush loss to Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian) on 5 June 2004, his own tag partner pinned after a top-rope Frog Splash. Teamed with Trevor Hextall and Tom Landis in a Meltdown main event win over Quinn Brown and Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian) on 25 August 2004, Hextall and Landis's own Game Misconduct heart-punch combination flooring Andrew Tucker for the pin. Teamed with Trevor Hextall and Kari Stevens in a losing intergender six-way against Fury (Rage, Spice) and Ami Tran by pinfall on 6 October 2004. Teamed with Trevor Hextall as Team Canada in a no-contest against the Hands of Death (Caliban, Serge Annis) on 13 November 2004, broke a hockey stick across Caliban's knee mid-match before the bout dissolved into a mass brawl. Teamed with Trevor Hextall and Scott Daniels as the Pride, beating Amity (the One-Winged Angel, Rage, Spice) in the Bluff City Streetfight main event on 27 November 2004 after Derek Martin turned on the One-Winged Angel to score the pinfall. Joined Trevor Hextall in beating down a fallen "Hentai" Ryu Osawa after Hextall's own pinfall win on 1 December 2004, broken up by a returning "Showtime" Rick Marley. On 11 December 2004, brawled backstage with Spice in a Pride-Fury melee, then attacked an intervening Ryu Osawa. Was part of the Pride's own ringside entrance and locker-room scenes on 28 May 2005, celebrating the group's Rise to Power sweep and welcoming the returning Brett Greene alongside the rest of the group.

notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2003: #21, tagged UWF; 2004: #79, tagged UWF, the list's own prior-year note reading (#21). caption: Held a place in the RSPWF Top 200 for two editions running, highest at #21 in 2003 and lowest at #79 in 2004.

tenures.note: "The Drunken Icon," a member of the Fraternity Boys; volunteered from the crowd as a same-night replacement challenger for an injured Sean Watts and pinned champion Uriah Hawkins to win the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World on 9 August 2003. Defended the title against Michael Bonn in his hometown of Pittsburgh on 4 October 2003; the referee waved off a Bonn pinfall for a foot on the ropes, and no decision was ever rendered after Bonn beat down the referee, McKenzie, and O'Brien. Teamed with Brian McKenzie as the Fraternity Boys in a Las Vegas Street Fight loss to the Arcana on 15 November 2003, handcuffed to the crowd barrier by Virginia St. Ursula and Michael Bonn before the finish. Retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World again on 20 December 2003, pinning Quinn Brown with an accidental Ace Crusher counter; Michael Bonn interrupted the pre-match introductions by beating a captive Brian McKenzie on camera, and the two brawled through the arena for the rest of the broadcast, ending with Bonn piledriving O'Brien onto a steel chair in the lobby. Shared a strip-club scene with a visibly drunk Victor Frost on 19 May 2004 ahead of their own upcoming Gold Rush match, then lost a four corners contenders match to the One-Winged Angel, driven down by a Revelator alongside two other fallen men for the pin. Substituted into a tag confrontation against Serge Annis and Caliban on 29 May 2004 alongside Brian McKenzie, breaking a Jalapeño Pepper Beer bottle over Caliban's head before Caliban pinned McKenzie for the loss; substituted again for the injured McKenzie in the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship match later the same night, beating champion Victor Frost by countout when Frost abandoned the match to chase a returning Quinn Brown, the title not changing hands. Lost a UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World challenge to champion One-Winged Angel on 22 September 2004 in a friendly MBC-reunion contest, caught with the Heavenly Wind and Hell's Halo combination; embraced the champion afterward. Baited tag partner Brian McKenzie backstage on 27 November 2004 over his own lack of ring time, then threw a cup of Chai in McKenzie's face; needled Donna Tetreault about her relationship with McKenzie before wishing the couple well. Held up a protest sign at ringside during Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie's own mixed tag win on 11 December 2004; McKenzie grabbed the sign and used it on Paul Wong. Ambushed Caliban with a steel chair backstage and brawled with Serge Annis through a door on 28 May 2005, then lost a handicap match to both Hands of Death members by pinfall (the Epitomizer) after a wild brawl that put both men through a table off a balcony. Accepted a backstage apology and a replacement laptop from Michael Bonn on 8 June 2005, with Virginia St. Ursula and Ryu Osawa looking on, then traded online-game banter with the pair; ambushed Ravnos Romani at ringside with a steel-chair Conchairto alongside Brian McKenzie on 11 June 2005 during the non-title four corners tag main event, until Niklos Romani drove both Fraternity Boys off with a springboard splash. Beat Brian McKenzie at Dance Dance Revolution in an arcade on 22 June 2005 and traded barbs with Donna Tetreault over training methods. Shared a beer and a truce with Alex Martinez backstage on 6 July 2005 after their own best-two-out-of-three-falls Road to the Gold final. Sang a comedic hockey song backstage ahead of facing Marcus Nuit on 23 July 2005, then lost the Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament/Unified Television Championship match by pinfall (a Falcon Arrow). Joined Brian McKenzie and Alex Kidd in running off the Illuminati at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, smashing beer bottles over Luke Kinsey and L. Dan Dee during a CareerBuilder.com-themed confrontation. Joined Donna Tetreault and Keith Marshall backstage at Cupid's Revenge on 14 February 2006, plotting elaborate revenge on the returning Simon O'Neal over a shell-shocked Brian McKenzie. Brawled with Paul Wong at ringside throughout Donna Tetreault's own No Disqualification match with Simon O'Neal on 18 March 2006.

name: "Hellraiser" Tom Landis
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2000: #132, tagged UWF; 2001: #62, tagged AEWA, MBC. The poll billed this wrestler more than one way across its editions: also as "Tom Landis". Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Climbed the RSPWF Top 200 across two editions, from #132 in 2000 to #62 in 2001.

tenures.note: Billed from Chicago, Illinois, a former UWF Heavyweight Champion of the World; challenged Paul Wong for the UWF Rampage Championship and lost when his own allies, Team Canada, interfered and were disqualified on 9 August 2003. Won the 30 August 2003 tag team main event with Scott Daniels over Quinn Brown and Alex Kidd, exposing a turnbuckle to hit Kidd with a Crossed-Arms Bomb. His 24 September 2003 singles match against Cameron Black was thrown out as a no-contest when Serge Annis attacked the Pride. Teamed with Scott Daniels and Team Canada as the Pride in a non-title, count-out loss on 22 October 2003, after Paul Wong turned Kari Stevens's own pepper spray back on him. Entered the 17 December 2003 battle royal, eliminated by Cameron Black with a right hand. Married to Tara Marshall; lost an intergender tag match with her on 24 March 2004 to Alex Kidd and Alicia Powers, pinned after Kidd's Somersault Bulldog set up Powers's own cover. Teamed with Team Canada (Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski) in a Meltdown main event win over Quinn Brown and Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker and Mike Sebastian) on 25 August 2004, his own Hextall-assisted Game Misconduct heart-punch flooring Andrew Tucker for the pin; manager Kari Stevens's own salt throw was turned back on her by Quinn Brown. Interfered repeatedly for the Pride during the Bluff City Streetfight main event on 27 November 2004, supplying weapons and blindsiding the One-Winged Angel, before a mystery attacker disguised as a fan shattered Landis's own crutch over his bad leg and DDTed him. Welcomed "Dead End" Derek Martin to the Pride on 11 December 2004 and taunted Shaun Borders, his own recent attacker, over the microphone. Beat a diminutive stand-in sent in Shaun Borders's own place by pinfall (a modified Diamond Dust) on 28 May 2005, having set up the mismatch himself; the genuine Shaun Borders never appeared. Chose Trey DaMann as Shaun Borders's own opponent on 6 July 2005, then attacked Borders with Borders's own Diamond Dust finisher after Borders appeared to have the match won, handing DaMann the pin. Lost to Rick Marley, Borders's own chosen opponent, by pinfall (the Limelight) in the companion match, after the Mercenary and Borders each separately interfered. Introduced as one half of the Cornerstones with Daniel Kidd on 23 July 2005, challenging Shaun Borders to a Gold Rush match; interfered at ringside during the main event tag match without officially entering it. Lost to "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn by pinfall on 3 August 2005 after Shaun Borders interfered at ringside and hurled him back into a Skyscreamer, then struck him with the Diamond Dust after the bell; his own Cornerstones interference later helped cost tag partner Daniel Kidd the main-card bout with Alex Martinez. Interfered as one of the Cornerstones in the North American Tag Team title match on 18 March 2006, then confronted Colby Greene on the interview platform and was driven off by a returning Madison J. Valentine; also cost Juan Vasquez's debut match a clean finish before Don't Go There turned the tables on him.

name: Tragedy
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1999: #148, tagged UWF; 2000: #94, tagged UWF; 2001: #34, tagged MBC, UWF; 2003: #53, tagged UWF, MBC. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Climbed the RSPWF Top 200 across four editions, from #148 in 1999 to #53 in 2003.

tenures.note: Original member of the Dark Harlequins, billed as having held nine separate UWF championships; pinned Derek Irvin with the Sleepy Hollow Driver in a non-title singles match on 9 August 2003 and announced designs on the North American Heavyweight Championship. Challenged for that title against champion Eugene Robinson on 30 August 2003, fought to a draw after Derek Irvin's interference forced a double stoppage. Teamed with Robinson and Irvin in a losing six-man tag on 4 October 2003, disqualified when Irvin struck him with a steel chair; knocked Irvin back down with the Sleepy Hollow Driver after the bell. Lost to Victor Frost by pinfall on 12 November 2003. Entered the 17 December 2003 battle royal, eliminated together with Alex Kidd when Avanter snapmared Kidd into him. Returned on 29 May 2004 to challenge Uriah Hawkins for the UWF Rampage Championship, the match ruled a no-contest after Pierce Bleed attacked the referee while Tragedy still had the Tragic Ending locked on; told a reporter afterward that he needed no help from the promotion's ownership to win championships. Lost to "Mr. Excitement" Alex Extreme by pinfall on 25 August 2004 after an implant DDT and a springboard finisher; his wife, Comedy, accompanied him, and Rodney distracted him mid-match by slapping Comedy and fleeing.

tenures.source: A cross-promotional main event on a rival federation's own pay-per-view, "Southern Pride" (22 March 1999), refereed by Bruno Riggs.
tenures.note: Defended the UWF World Cruiserweight Championship in a cross-promotional main event against that rival federation's own top contender on its 22 March 1999 pay-per-view, going to the ropes for a near-fall late in the bout before a returning outside wrestler, billed by the broadcast as part of an "invasion" from a further, unrelated federation, struck the challenger with a folding chair behind the referee's back; Tragedy retained on the resulting pinfall.

name: Uriah Hawkins
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2003: #60, tagged UWF, MBC, LEW; 2004: #101, tagged UWF, the list's own prior-year note reading (#61). Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Held a place in the RSPWF Top 200 for two editions running, highest at #60 in 2003 and lowest at #101 in 2004.

tenures.note: Won the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World at Gold Rush 2003; lost the title in his first defense two and a half weeks later, breaking his arm on a botched moonsault fall against a same-night replacement challenger, Chris O'Brien. Billed as the reigning UWF Rampage Champion on 24 March 2004, retaining against "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall (a small package) after both men traded finishing-move attempts; "The Doomsayer" Kyle Lee ran off Martin's post-match chair attack. No surviving document in the held record states when or how Hawkins won the Rampage Championship from its own prior record holder, the One-Winged Angel. Retained the UWF Rampage Championship again on 15 May 2004 in a three-way dance, sneaking in behind challengers Troy Grace and Quinn Brown as they collided and catching both with a double DDT for the pin. Retained the UWF Rampage Championship again on 29 May 2004 when a title defense against Tragedy was ruled a no-contest after Pierce Bleed attacked the referee while Tragedy still had the Tragic Ending locked on; Bleed then challenged him to a title-versus-career match at Gold Rush with T.D. Swagger as special referee. Retained the UWF Rampage Championship at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, pinning Pierce Bleed with a Suicide DDT after special referee T.D. Swagger restarted the match, having ruled out an illegal cordless-microphone shot; Bleed's own UWF contract was voided under the match's own title-versus-contract stipulation. Lost the UWF Rampage Championship to Jamie Underwood by pinfall on 28 August 2004, blindsided by a run-in Papa Legba's own Ragga Bomb moments before Underwood's small package; broke up Derek Martin's own backstage chair attack on Alex Kidd earlier the same show. Fought Papa Legba to a double countout in a UWF Meltdown Championship tournament opener on 8 September 2004, seconded by manager Holly Williams. Lost a tag match alongside Alex Kidd to Scott "Hotspot" Daniels and a substituting "Dead End" Derek Martin on 18 September 2004, seconded by manager Holly Williams. Won the main event over "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall (an Oklahoma side roll) on 2 October 2004, capitalizing on a leg he had worked over throughout the match after Martin's own knee buckled mid-charge; cut a pre-match promo on respect in professional wrestling, naming Martin directly. Lost a Tower of Doom cage match on 30 October 2004 alongside Quinn Brown, Alex Extreme, and Alex Martinez to the team of Edmond Winston IV, Victor Frost, Papa Legba, and Luke Kinsey, who escaped the structure first when Alex Martinez inadvertently threw Winston clear of the cage; joined the others in a post-bell beatdown of Winston with his own solid gold knuckles. Lost a UWF North American Heavyweight Championship challenge to champion "Violent" Victor Frost by pinfall on 17 November 2004, driving his own head into the mat attempting a Suicide DDT after Frost hung on to the top rope. Lost a hard-fought grudge match to Papa Legba by pinfall (Roots) on 11 December 2004, the two shaking hands afterward despite their own history.

name: Bliss
caption: A Bod Squad member and former UWF Women's Champion who fell short in a rematch against Stephanie Harper after Erin McCoys blocked a teammate's interference.

tenures.note: Billed from Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, New York, a former UWF Women's Champion and Bod Squad member; lost a UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World match to Stephanie Harper. Teamed with Tara "Sunburst" Marshall as the Bod Squad on 22 October 2003, pinning Marissa Monet with a DDT in a win over Monet and Sierra Browne. Teamed with Tara "Sunburst" Marshall as the Bod Squad in a win by disqualification over the Furies (Leslie Hernandez, Angel) on 12 November 2003, earning a future UWF Women's Tag Team Championship shot.

name: "The First American Badass" Brian McKenzie
caption: One-half of the Fraternity Boys, pinned in a non-title cruiserweight bout and again in a hometown-Pittsburgh intergender tag two weeks later.

tenures.note: A member of the Fraternity Boys alongside Chris O'Brien; lost a non-title cruiserweight contest to Michael Bonn on 30 August 2003, then lost the Meltdown main event intergender tag match in his hometown of Pittsburgh, pinned by Donna Tetreault after Simon O'Neal tricked his own partner, Tara Smith, into slapping him. Challenged the One-Winged Angel for the UWF Rampage Championship on 15 November 2003, pinned after being distracted by Virginia St. Ursula's bottle of Bailey's Irish Cream. Teamed with Chris O'Brien as the Fraternity Boys the same night in a Las Vegas Street Fight loss to the Arcana (Niklos and Ravnos Romani), pinned by a swinging DDT. Entered the 17 December 2003 battle royal, eliminated by Alex Kidd's skin-the-cat over the top rope. Assaulted backstage by Michael Bonn on 20 December 2003 while his own tag partner Chris O'Brien wrestled the Cruiserweight title match, dragged in front of the production camera and beaten with a flashlight; did not compete in a structured match that night. Returned on 29 May 2004 teaming with Chris O'Brien against Serge Annis and Caliban in a tag confrontation, pinned after Caliban caught him on an outstretched knee off a Near Death Experience superplex; too hurt to make his own scheduled UWF North American Heavyweight Championship challenge later the same night, replaced by O'Brien. Lost a UWF Meltdown Championship tournament opener to Vyolynce by pinfall (Oblivion) on 8 September 2004, then cost Vyolynce's semifinal opponent Paul Wong the match by running in and drawing a disqualification. Lost a UWF Rampage Championship challenge to champion "Showtime" Rick Marley by countout on 30 October 2004, walking out mid-match to save tag partner Chris O'Brien from a backstage beating by Michael Bonn. Gave girlfriend Donna Tetreault a foot rub backstage on 27 November 2004, then declared he would start booking his own matches after being goaded by tag partner Chris O'Brien and Tetreault herself. Worked out backstage with Keith Marshall on 1 December 2004 ahead of his own Rampage tag match, then joined Chris O'Brien in outrage over a new caffeinated Budweiser variant. On 11 December 2004, beat Paul Wong by pinfall with Donna Tetreault, pinning Wong himself after Tetreault planted a pair of smuggled brass knuckles on him mid-match; Chris O'Brien's own ringside protest sign was used as a weapon on Wong along the way. Was drugged by girlfriend Donna Tetreault before Chris O'Brien's own handicap match with the Hands of Death on 28 May 2005 and spent the rest of the broadcast passed out in her locker room. Ambushed Ravnos Romani at ringside with a steel-chair Conchairto alongside Chris O'Brien on 11 June 2005 during the non-title four corners tag main event, taunting the announce table about the Fraternity Boys' own need for attention. Lost a Road to the Gold qualifier to the Mercenary on 22 June 2005 after being jumped in the aisle by the Romanis and distracted mid-match by a confrontation between Chris O'Brien and Rick Marley; earlier lost a game of Dance Dance Revolution to Chris O'Brien at an arcade and punched a heckler. Assaulted Stephanie Harper backstage on 3 August 2005 after she interfered in a match involving girlfriend Donna Tetreault; brawled with the Illuminati alongside Chris O'Brien and Alex Kidd at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, then ambushed Paul Wong with Tetreault backstage. Teamed with Donna Tetreault to win the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament's opening round on 14 February 2006 with a Hart Attack clothesline on Lolita Love, then was eliminated in the finals alongside Tetreault by Brett Greene and Alex Extreme. Charged the ring to confront a returning Simon O'Neal on 18 March 2006 and brawled with him through most of Donna Tetreault's own No Disqualification match, pinned by O'Neal's loaded-glove fistdrop moments before Tetreault stole the win herself.

name: "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict
caption: "Dirty Darrin" Kisler's student, fought the Mockingbird Nina Grimsson to a time-limit draw in a match that set up a three-way Women's Championship defense.

tenures.note: Fought Nina Grimsson to a fifteen-minute time-limit draw, earning both women a three-way UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World shot against Stephanie Harper the following week. Lost that three-way title match on 25 October 2003, pinned by champion Stephanie Harper's Fallen Star. Lost to Tara Smith by pinfall on 12 November 2003, despite nearly winning with a Blissful Awakening fishermanbuster. Beat Brianna Landis, Tara Marshall's own personal assistant and sister-in-law, by referee stoppage on 21 March 2004 after Marshall sent Landis in as a last-minute substitute opponent; locked on a DDT into leg scissors until the official called the match. Beat "Wildfire" Leslie Hernandez by pinfall on 5 May 2004 with her feet on the ropes, then applied a post-match Morbid Sting until Arielle Starr ran in and traded blows with her. Lost to Arielle Starr by pinfall at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, caught by the Bedazzler enzuigiri and a top-rope Skytwister Press after her own legdrop off the top rope missed. Returned from a hiatus following a loss to Arielle Starr at Gold Rush and lost to Moira Faith by pinfall (a rolling Diamond Dust ace crusher) on 25 May 2005, then attacked Faith after the bell, opening a cut above her eye. Broke into the Love Sisters' own locker room on 11 June 2005 and helped Moira Faith beat down both sisters ahead of their own Women's Tag Team Championship match, acting on the order of a man addressed as Caine. Plotted against the Love Sisters and a returning Naomi Ishikawa with Moira Faith over Lolita Love's own kidnapped cat, Mr. Boo Boo, on 6 July 2005, then lost to the Misfits (Dalbello Rage, Marissa Monet) alongside Faith in the Kindred's own debut tag match, pinned by Marissa Monet's Mischief Maker. Joined Moira Faith and Caine Tainer in cornering and threatening Lolita Love in a backstage bathroom on 20 July 2005, handing Moira a makeshift knife fashioned from broken mirror glass. Tortured a captive Lolita Love on camera with cousin Moira Faith on 3 August 2005; knocked out with a steel chair by cousin Sonya Benedict during a no-contest handicap six-woman tag on 6 August 2005. Teamed with Moira Faith as the Kindred in a losing effort against "Firebird" Katie Smith and "Tornado" Tara Smith on 7 June 2006, pinned by Tara Smith's own Arizona Rattler after a long heat segment on Katie Smith. Beat Samantha Daniels by pinfall (a heel kick into a rollup) in a return to singles competition on 28 April 2007, with Donna Tetreault's repeated ringside taunting breaking Daniels's own concentration late in the match; introduced afterward as the newest member of Amity by "Supervixen" Ami Tran, then joined Tran in accepting a future title challenge from Women's North American Champion Sonya Benedict, her own cousin. Was separately confronted backstage the same night by estranged brothers Jacen and Ronan Benedict, the War Hounds, who urged her to leave Darrin Kisler's Bloodhorn faction; she held a knife to Jacen's throat without following through and refused their appeal.

name: Erik Grimsson
caption: The smaller half of the headbanging tag team the Sons of Cacaphony, flooring the Harlequins' Chaos with an overhand right cross in an upset win.

tenures.note: Teamed with his brother Chad as the Sons of Cacaphony, upsetting the former tag champions the Harlequins. Lost a non-title tag match to the Privateers on 25 October 2003 when Edward Drake, not the legal man, struck Chad with a hidden lead weight for an illegal pin. Teamed with brother Chad in the Tower of Doom on 15 November 2003, escaping the cage first among his own teammates but taking a battering from Sabbat Justice on the arena floor afterward; the pair's escape as a complete team won them the UWF North American Tag Team Championship away from their own side's champions, the Ghost Dancers. The first man eliminated from the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match, pinned by Bob Jablonski after manager Kari Stevens cracked him with a hockey stick behind the referee's back. Competed in the six-man tag on 10 March 2004, part of the losing side against Team Canada and Scott Daniels after two masked interlopers ambushed the match. Retained the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with brother Chad on 21 March 2004 over the Universal Powers, the Sky Hammer combination finishing Bobby Lincoln after both teams traded dives to the floor. Teamed with Michael Keening in a scrambled-partners tag on 5 May 2004 against Niklos Romani and Todd Franklin; the bout ended as a no-contest after Franklin turned on his own partner and finished Grimsson himself with a New Horizon Line. Lost the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with brother Chad on 28 August 2004 in a street fight against the Universal Powers, knocked out by an unidentified masked interloper from inside a locker-room closet before Todd Franklin's superkick finished him for the pin; the Privateers separately ambushed Chad at ringside during the same match. Teamed with brother Chad and Alex Martinez to beat the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) and Randall Osbourne on 22 September 2004, combining with Martinez for a version of the Harlequins' own Reality Check on Todd Franklin for the pin. Teamed with brother Chad in a losing effort against "Hentai" Ryu Osawa and Michael Bonn by disqualification on 16 October 2004, the Sons of Cacaphony's own side disqualified after Erik attacked a non-competing Jacob Drake at ringside; the finish set off a building-wide brawl that ultimately knocked the broadcast off the air, Erik and Michael Augustine's own fight atop the production truck among the last scenes shown. Teamed with Chad Grimsson as the Sons of Cacaphony in a no-contest against Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian) on 17 November 2004, taken out by the Privateers' own High-Seas Shipwreck when they ran in to end the match. Ran in with brother Chad and Alex Extreme to save Lisa Drake from a beating by the Youngbloods on 27 November 2004, then helped carry her out on a makeshift gurney; threatened the Privateers with a UWF World Tag Team Championship challenge, set for Rise to Power alongside Chad. Retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship with brother Chad over the Privateers by pinfall (an inverted backslide DDT, the Metal Meltdown) on 28 May 2005, after interference from Fury (Rage, Spice) at ringside disrupted the challengers. Helped break up a post-match beatdown of Alex Extreme and Jason Keening on 11 June 2005 alongside Alex Martinez, then teamed with brother Chad in a non-title four corners tag main event, eliminated by disqualification after Caliban struck both Grimssons with a steel chair. Drank with the Mercenary, Alex Extreme, and Alex Martinez at a Memphis club on 22 June 2005, vowing revenge on the Hands of Death alongside brother Chad. Berated by Alex Extreme backstage on 20 July 2005 over the loss of the World Tag Team Championship. Kidnapped and chained up Caliban inside the Descent Into Hell structure on 23 July 2005, challenging the Hands of Death to defend the tag titles in that match at Gold Rush. Teamed with brother Chad and Corey Irons to beat the Hands of Death and Trey DaMann by pinfall on 3 August 2005, Irons pinning Caliban; called out the Hands of Death with Chad at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005 and was singed by Serge Annis's own pyrotechnics when no confrontation came.

name: Chad Grimsson
caption: The larger half of the headbanging tag team the Sons of Cacaphony, closing out an upset win over the former champions the Harlequins with a release German suplex.

tenures.note: Teamed with his brother Erik as the Sons of Cacaphony, upsetting the former tag champions the Harlequins. Lost a non-title tag match to the Privateers on 25 October 2003, pinned by Edward Drake's lead-weight-assisted powerbomb while Drake was not the legal man. Teamed with brother Erik in the Tower of Doom on 15 November 2003, delayed from escaping the cage by Trevor Hextall while Sabbat Justice beat down his brother outside; once free, the pair's escape as a complete team won them the UWF North American Tag Team Championship away from their own side's champions, the Ghost Dancers. Ambushed by Sabbat Justice at ringside and dropped neck-first onto exposed concrete by Avanter during the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match; teammate Edmond Winston IV spitefully tagged him back in on an injured neck as revenge for an earlier slight, and Michael Augustine pinned him with an Impact DDT for the elimination. Appeared backstage on 10 March 2004, upset about his own recent break-up with Sonya Benedict but not competing. Retained the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with brother Erik on 21 March 2004 over the Universal Powers, hitting a mammoth dive to the floor before the Sky Hammer finished Bobby Lincoln. Lost to "The Savior" Jamie Underwood by pinfall on 19 May 2004 after ex-girlfriend Sonya Benedict held his leg down for the cover, following a backstage confrontation between the two earlier that night. Lost the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with brother Erik on 28 August 2004 in a street fight against the Universal Powers, ambushed at ringside by the Privateers before an unidentified masked interloper knocked Erik out and Todd Franklin's superkick finished him for the pin. Teamed with brother Erik and Alex Martinez to beat the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) and Randall Osbourne on 22 September 2004, helping isolate Todd Franklin before Erik and Martinez finished him with a version of the Harlequins' own Reality Check. Teamed with brother Erik in a losing effort against "Hentai" Ryu Osawa and Michael Bonn by disqualification on 16 October 2004, the Sons of Cacaphony's own side disqualified after Erik attacked a non-competing Jacob Drake at ringside, touching off a building-wide brawl that ultimately knocked the broadcast off the air. Teamed with Erik Grimsson as the Sons of Cacaphony in a no-contest against Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian) on 17 November 2004, ended after the Privateers ran in and hit Erik with the High-Seas Shipwreck. Ran in with brother Erik and Alex Extreme to save Lisa Drake from a beating by the Youngbloods on 27 November 2004, then helped carry her out on a makeshift gurney; agreed to a tentative alliance with Papa Legba backstage afterward. A UWF World Tag Team Championship challenge against the Privateers, alongside Erik, was announced for Rise to Power. Retained the UWF World Tag Team Championship with brother Erik over the Privateers by pinfall on 28 May 2005, after interference from Fury (Rage, Spice) at ringside disrupted the challengers. Discussed North American Champion Papa Legba's own sincerity with brother Erik backstage on 11 June 2005, helped break up a post-match beatdown of Alex Extreme and Jason Keening, then lost a non-title four corners tag main event by disqualification after Caliban struck both Grimssons with a steel chair. Drank with the Mercenary, Alex Extreme, and Alex Martinez at a Memphis club on 22 June 2005, vowing revenge on the Hands of Death alongside brother Erik. Berated by Alex Extreme backstage on 20 July 2005 over the lost tag titles, then lost to Trey DaMann by pinfall (a modified Trillion Dollar DDT) after nearly finishing him with a slingshot full nelson dragon suplex. Asked "War Machine" Corey Irons on 23 July 2005 to look after girlfriend Sonya Benedict against the Hands of Death while he and brother Erik focused on their own feud with Serge Annis and Caliban. Teamed with brother Erik and Corey Irons to beat the Hands of Death and Trey DaMann on 3 August 2005; called out the Hands of Death with Erik at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, the Unitron answering with a taunting nursery rhyme rather than a confrontation.

tenures.note: One-half of the Harlequins alongside Terror; pinned by the Sons of Cacaphony in an upset. Teamed with Terror against the Universal Powers on 19 May 2004, felled by a mafia kick from an unidentified interloper before Terror was finished with the Universal Elimination.

name: Simon O'Neal
caption: A self-styled "dirty bastard" who trains Donna Tetreault, tricking his own intergender tag partner Tara Smith into slapping Brian McKenzie for the winning distraction.

tenures.note: Teamed with his trainee Donna Tetreault to win the Meltdown main event intergender tag match over Brian McKenzie and Tara Smith. Challenged the One-Winged Angel for the UWF Rampage Championship on 25 October 2003, losing by pinfall after the two traded a loaded punch and a cane shot in a wild exchange. Entered the 17 December 2003 fifteen-man battle royal to crown the first UWF Meltdown Champion; his own elimination went unannounced by name. Coached and repeatedly interfered for Donna Tetreault as she won the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World from Stephanie Harper on 15 May 2004; a pair of brass knuckles was found at ringside afterward. Teamed with the new champion against Tigress and Papa Legba for the UWF Meltdown Championship on 19 May 2004, losing when Legba's top-rope splash caught them both. Lost to Taurus by pinfall on 6 October 2004 after collapsing under his own weight attempting a bodyslam. Returned to the UWF on 14 February 2006 with a solo Cupid's Revenge vignette recounting his own comeback, his tag partner Paul Wong's own injury while he was away, and his feud with Chris O'Brien, Brian McKenzie, and Donna Tetreault; ambushed a charging McKenzie in a No Disqualification match set up by Tetreault on 18 March 2006, hitting a loaded-glove fistdrop for an unofficial pin before Tetreault chair-shotted him from behind to steal the match, since the booking was against her, not McKenzie.

name: Donna Tetreault
caption: Simon O'Neal's trainee, scoring the deciding small package pinfall over Brian McKenzie in her partner's hometown of Pittsburgh.

tenures.note: Trained by Simon O'Neal; pinned Brian McKenzie with a small package to win the Meltdown main event intergender tag match. Beat Tara Smith by submission (Caress of Steel) in a non-title singles rematch on 22 October 2003, wrestling without Simon O'Neal at ringside for the first time. Challenged Stephanie Harper for the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World on 15 November 2003, wrestling without trainer Simon O'Neal at ringside after Vice-President Jessica Marshall barred him; submitted to the Texas Cloverleaf. Beat "Alluring" Arielle Starr by pinfall on 10 March 2004 with a Domination Day suplex after Myra Benedict's knife-wielding distraction gave her the opening; Simon O'Neal coached her from ringside beforehand on countering Starr's high-flying style. Beat "Wildfire" Leslie Hernandez by referee stoppage on 24 March 2004 after knocking her out with a ringside bucket, applying the Caress of Steel once Hernandez could no longer defend herself; Simon O'Neal and the Amazing Romanis brawled at ringside throughout. Won the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World from Stephanie Harper on 15 May 2004 with a somersault plancha followed by a pinfall as the referee's count on both women lapsed; brass knuckles were found at ringside afterward. Teamed with Simon O'Neal against Tigress and Papa Legba for the UWF Meltdown Championship on 19 May 2004, losing when Legba's top-rope splash caught both her and O'Neal at once. Retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World over Stephanie Harper by pinfall at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, using brass knuckles and then a foreign object hidden in her own bandana for the Caress of Steel; knocked out manager Simon O'Neal after he proposed marriage to her in the ring afterward. Retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship over Brianna Landis by pinfall (the Dominion Day windmill suplex) on 18 September 2004, aided by a distraction belt shot from Tara "Sunburst" Marshall. Wrestled a non-title six-woman tag alongside the Bod Squad against Sierra Browne and Team BATTLE*DREAM on 2 October 2004, sneaking into the match in a Greece cosplay disguise after her partners were forced to start a woman short; the match was lost when Sierra Browne's Truth Superkick finished Brianna Landis, and Tetreault ambushed Browne with the women's title belt afterward. Retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World over "Battle Princess" Misaki Ishikawa by disqualification on 16 October 2004 after Ishikawa was found with a taser at ringside; finished Ishikawa post-match with a Minnie Driver. Retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World over Kari Stevens by submission (a crossface, rubbing salt and lemon juice into a cut over Stevens's own eye) on 30 October 2004, having hidden a lemon wedge and salt of her own to counter Team Canada's own salt-throwing interference. A UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World defense against "Alluring" Arielle Starr on 13 November 2004 ended without a finish after Sierra Browne, Alicia Powers and "Tornado" Tara Smith ran in and a chain-loaded glove shot meant for Starr struck Brian McKenzie instead; Tetreault fled with the title still around her waist. Interfered at ringside during the Browne-Harper number one contendership match on 27 November 2004, first tripping Sierra Browne into a rollup loss that Stephanie Harper refused to accept, then tripping Browne again once the match was restarted; fled after Harper and Browne jointly turned on her. Beat Sierra Browne and Paul Wong with Brian McKenzie by pinfall on 11 December 2004, planting smuggled brass knuckles on McKenzie mid-match after a search failed to find them on her; dined beforehand with McKenzie, who revealed plans to dump his own Anheuser-Busch stock. Drugged boyfriend Brian McKenzie's own drink before Chris O'Brien's handicap match with the Hands of Death on 28 May 2005, then watched the beating from the back with amusement. Watched boyfriend Brian McKenzie lose a Dance Dance Revolution challenge to Chris O'Brien at an arcade on 22 June 2005, then broke up a brewing argument between the two Fraternity Boys. Lost a number-one contenders match to "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson on 20 July 2005 after the referee restarted the bout on Stephanie Harper's own insistence; was later told by Becky Byers and Harper that she would face Harper at Gold Rush under Blind Stipulation Rules. Backed boyfriend Brian McKenzie's backstage assault on Stephanie Harper on 3 August 2005; helped McKenzie ambush Paul Wong with a steel chair and brass knuckles on 6 August 2005, warning that Stephanie Harper's own Gold Rush stipulation match would not go her way. Teamed with Brian McKenzie to win the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament's opening round on 14 February 2006 over Dan Kidd and Kari Stevens and Lolita Love and DOOM!, then was eliminated in the finals alongside McKenzie by Brett Greene and Alex Extreme; earlier joined Chris O'Brien and Keith Marshall backstage plotting elaborate revenge on the returning Simon O'Neal. Set up and won a No Disqualification match against O'Neal on 18 March 2006, chair-shotting him from behind to steal the pinfall after Brian McKenzie had traded blows with him for much of the match.

tenures.note: A three-time former UWF World Heavyweight Champion returning from a two-year absence; teamed with Quinn Brown in a losing tag team main event against Scott Daniels and Tom Landis, pinned after Landis's exposed-turnbuckle Crossed-Arms Bomb. Teamed with Paul Wong, Youth Gone Wild, and Quinn Brown to a count-out win over the Pride on 22 October 2003. Attacked from behind backstage without provocation by Randall Osbourne on 12 November 2003, then wrestled Avanter to a disqualification finish the same night when the Grimssons and Alex Extreme ran in three-on-one. Entered the 17 December 2003 battle royal; his own elimination went unannounced by name. Attacked again from behind backstage without explanation by Randall Osbourne on 20 December 2003 and taken to a local hospital, before either man could compete that night. Challenged Papa Legba for the UWF Meltdown Championship on 10 March 2004 with wife Alicia Kidd at ringside; lost by pinfall (Ragga Bomb) after leaving the ring to check on his wife against a threatening Randall Osbourne, an opening Legba and interfering Tigress exploited. Assaulted Randall Osbourne before the 24 March 2004 steel cage main event, driving the cage door into his knee and forcing Osbourne to leave without ever entering the match. Teamed with wife Alicia Powers to beat Tom Landis and Tara Marshall in an intergender tag match the same night after his own Somersault Bulldog set up her pinfall; Randall Osbourne then brought out Kidd's own ex-wife, Cameo, who low-blowed Kidd and hairpulled Powers down. Teamed with Paul Wong and "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee against Team Canada and Scott Daniels on 15 May 2004 in a six-man tag that ended without a decision amid a mass brawl; carried an injured Paul Wong from his own locker room to a hospital afterward alongside Kyle Lee, after Serge Annis and Caliban attacked him. Beat Randall Osbourne by pinfall (a full nelson bulldog) at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004 in a personal grudge match complicated by Osbourne's manager, Kidd's own ex-wife Cameo, surviving a Tree of Woe facebite and a Somersault Bulldog that also knocked out Cameo. Pinned by the Hands of Death's own Near Death Experience in a losing steel cage main event on 28 August 2004 after tag partner Kyle Lee escaped the cage but could not return in time to help. Lost a tag match alongside Uriah Hawkins to Scott "Hotspot" Daniels and a substituting "Dead End" Derek Martin on 18 September 2004, pinned by Martin's own End chokeslam despite having tagged out moments before. Teamed with Sabbath in a losing effort against Jamie Underwood and "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall on 30 October 2004, Underwood countering Sabbath's own Coffin Breaker II attempt for the pin; beaten down with steel chairs afterward alongside Sabbath. Lost a Tuxedo Death Match to Edmond Winston IV on 13 November 2004, unable to answer referee Ingraham's ten count after a cobra clutch suplex, in a brutal brawl that spilled from the ring to Winston's own limousine. Returned from injury to save the One-Winged Angel from a Pridebreaker on 11 December 2004, hitting a somersault bulldog on both Scott Daniels and Derek Martin before the Pride retreated; tried and failed afterward to free Marissa Monet and Pizzazz from their own skybox chains. Fought Luke Kinsey to a double countout on 11 June 2005, then was surrounded by the Illuminati before Kinsey called them off and let him leave with his wife and manager, Alicia Powers. Beat Andrew "Flash" Tucker by pinfall (a full nelson bulldog) on 20 July 2005. Responded to Illuminati taunts on 23 July 2005 by challenging Luke Kinsey and the whole stable to a Gold Rush match, saying he would take on all four if needed. Ran in to help fend off Illuminati interference in the Underwood/Vyolynce match on 3 August 2005; returned to challenge the entire Illuminati at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, teaming with the Fraternity Boys to run the group off after German-suplexing Luke Kinsey into a corner. Teamed with "Tornado" Tara Smith in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, eliminated by Brett Greene's superbomb after warning Greene backstage to take care of wife and tag partner Alicia Powers. Teamed with wife Alicia Powers to beat Kari Stevens and "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall on 7 June 2006. Ran in to help John Shock against Madison J. Valentine and Colby Greene after Shock's own three-way dance win on 28 April 2007, then was clipped from behind and put in a scorpion deathlock by a still-unidentified masked man before all three beat down both fallen men.

Teamed with the Kindred in a no-contest handicap six-woman tag against Sonya Benedict and Leanna Love on 6 August 2005, fleeing backstage after Sonya Benedict came after her with a steel chair. Lost an I Quit match to Sonya Benedict on 18 March 2006 by referee stoppage after a Burning Sunset Flip to the arena floor left her unable to continue; never said the words despite repeated chair shots, headbutts, and a broken nose, and was stretchered out.

tenures.note: Billed from Kansas City, Missouri; lost a non-title singles match to Vyolynce of Sabbat Justice by referee stoppage after Vyolynce needled him over his girlfriend, Tawni Northern. Teamed with Alex Extreme against Papa Legba and Avanter on 22 October 2003 in a match that ended without a decision after Osbourne turned on his own partner mid-match and left, and Sabbat Justice beat Extreme down five-on-one. Attacked a returning Alex Kidd from behind backstage without provocation on 12 November 2003, then challenged Kyle Lee for the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship the same night, disqualified for repeatedly biting the champion's forehead. Attacked a returning Alex Kidd from behind backstage without explanation for a second consecutive show on 20 December 2003, sending Kidd to a local hospital. Teamed with Nina Grimsson later that night in a losing intergender tag match against Avanter and Angel, driving Grimsson himself down repeatedly with a full-nelson suplex and a full-nelson backbreaker until she began coughing up blood and the referee stopped the match. Threatened Alicia Kidd at ringside during Alex Kidd's own Meltdown Championship challenge on 10 March 2004, distracting Kidd long enough for champion Papa Legba to score the pinfall. Entered a scheduled three-way for the UWF Meltdown Championship on 21 March 2004 that never started after Legba attacked both challengers with a chair before the bell and left; a cage-match rematch was announced for the following week. Lost to Alex Kidd by pinfall at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004 in a personal grudge match, caught with a full nelson bulldog after a Tree of Woe facebite and two Somersault Bulldogs; manager Cameo, Kidd's own ex-wife, was knocked unconscious by the first Somersault Bulldog. Lost to "Last American Badass" Alex Martinez by pinfall (a Firebomb Chokeslam) on 25 August 2004 despite a Tree of Woe facebite; manager Cameo's own distraction went for nothing. Lost a UWF Meltdown Championship tournament opener to Paul Wong by pinfall (a lariat) on 8 September 2004, seconded by Cameo. Lost alongside the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) to the Sons of Cacaphony and Alex Martinez on 22 September 2004, seconded again by Cameo. Lost to Luke Kinsey by pinfall (the Lowlife Driver, an inverted DDT) on 3 November 2004 after nearly pulling Kinsey from the ring, seconded at ringside by Cameo.

tenures.note: Billed from North Brookfield, Massachusetts, managed by Virginia St. Ursula; pinned Brian McKenzie with a top-rope 450 splash in a non-title cruiserweight contest. Fought newcomer November to a double-disqualification draw in a non-title match on 24 March 2004, now wrestling without a manager at ringside; Jamie Underwood and the One-Winged Angel both ran in before the finish. Lost the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World to One-Winged Angel by pinfall at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, caught in an uranage counter off his own Deadfall attempt and then a top-rope Hell's Halo; demanded a title rematch backstage afterward while trashing his own locker room. Lost his own Gold Rush rematch for the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World to One-Winged Angel by pinfall on 28 August 2004, his own top-rope hurricanrana reversed into the Revelator; attacked Angel with the title belt afterward until a thrown water bottle drew him into the crowd, where "Hentai" Ryu Osawa clotheslined him and challenged him to a career-versus-career match, approved by Jessica Marshall for the following week. Lost a no-disqualification Career Paths match to "Hentai" Ryu Osawa by pinfall (an underhook sit-down powerbomb) on 18 September 2004, forced into a tag team with him under the match's own stipulation; manager Virginia St. Ursula pulled a chair away from him mid-match, and he stormed off after accusing her of betrayal. Teamed with "Hentai" Ryu Osawa, forced into the pairing by the terms of his own prior loss to Osawa, to beat the Sons of Cacaphony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) by disqualification on 16 October 2004 in the pair's own first match together. Lost a UWF Meltdown Championship challenge to Tigress by disqualification on 3 November 2004, after a six-wrestler UWF tryout group (revealed to be led by a disguised T.D. Swagger) ran in and beat him down. Stood at the entrance and refused to help tag partner "Hentai" Ryu Osawa as Team Canada beat him down after Osawa's own loss on 1 December 2004. Apologized to Chris O'Brien for a prior beatdown on 8 June 2005, with manager Virginia St. Ursula and tag partner Ryu Osawa looking on, and gave O'Brien a replacement laptop; O'Brien accepted the apology. Grabbed tag partner Ryu Osawa by the collar over a joking remark about manager Virginia St. Ursula's own legs on 22 June 2005, then accompanied Osawa to his own Road to the Gold qualifier. Lost to Youth Gone Wild in the Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament's own first round on 6 July 2005, a hard-fought, mutually respectful contest that ended with a top-rope Wildflyer moonsault; told Virginia beforehand that he needed to prove he had changed since Rise to Power, and learned from Ryu Osawa that Osawa had won naming rights to their own still-unnamed tag team. Beat "Hellraiser" Tom Landis by pinfall (a Skyscreamer) on 3 August 2005 with an assist from Shaun Borders, who hurled Landis back into the move. Tripped Cornerstone Daniel Kidd during Juan Vasquez's debut match on 18 March 2006, turning back a Cornerstones interference attempt alongside tag partner Ryu Osawa.

tenures.note: Billed from Chicago, Illinois, a member of the Pride; teamed with Tom Landis to win the tag team main event over Quinn Brown and Alex Kidd, pinning Brown with the Before the Fall piledriver after a low blow. Also appeared on the following Meltdown, joining the Pride's attack on Serge Annis without competing in a structured match. Teamed with Tom Landis and Team Canada as the Pride in a non-title, count-out loss on 22 October 2003. Beat Paul Wong by pinfall (Pridebreaker) on 15 November 2003 with a low blow and his feet on the ropes, then challenged Quinn Brown to a sixty-minute Iron Man match at Eve of Destruction. Challenged the One-Winged Angel for the UWF Rampage Championship on 20 December 2003, knocking out the referee and appearing to score an unofficial pinfall of his own before Quinn Brown's entrance music distracted him long enough for the champion to retain with the Revelator; Brown then attacked him with a baseball bat and challenged him to an Iron Man match at Eve of Destruction. Teamed with Team Canada (Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski) on 10 March 2004 in a six-man tag win over the Ghost Dancers and Erik Grimsson, scoring the pinfall on Michael Keening after two unidentified men in suits ambushed Team Canada's opponents; also met privately and cordially with new owner Edmond Winston IV, who told him his own claim on Michael Augustine's UWF World Heavyweight Championship came first. Teamed with Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski again against Alex Kidd, Paul Wong, and "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee on 15 May 2004 in a six-man tag that ended without a decision amid a mass brawl; accepted debuting Alex Martinez's own in-ring challenge for Gold Rush after Vice-President Jessica Marshall made it a pay-per-view attraction. Lost to Alex Martinez by pinfall in a Gold Rush dream match on 5 June 2004 despite a low blow, a brass-knuckles punch, two steel chair shots and a Pridebreaker, caught with a Firebomb Chokeslam after a second Pridebreaker attempt was blocked. Lost to Jason Keening by pinfall (an inside cradle) on 28 August 2004, then attacked him after the bell with a Pridebreaker until a masked "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas -- Michael Keening's own attacker from Gold Rush -- interrupted; drove Douglas from the ring himself, calling it his own house rather than Keening's. Beat Alex Kidd and Uriah Hawkins by pinfall alongside a substituting "Dead End" Derek Martin on 18 September 2004 after tag partner Tom Landis was hospitalized in a backstage crowbar attack by "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas. Fought Chris Douglas to a double disqualification on 2 October 2004 under special guest referee Jason Keening, who ended the match himself and clotheslined both men from the ring after being caught between their blows; offered "Dead End" Derek Martin a spot in the Pride later the same show, which Martin turned down. Won a three-way dance over "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas and Jason Keening on 16 October 2004, stealing a pinfall on Keening after Keening and Douglas collided head-first. Fought "Agony" Michael Augustine to a no-contest on 3 November 2004 after Allison Ivey and Kari Stevens both struck their own man's opponent with a chair and Amity (One-Winged Angel, Spice, Rage) ran in on both wrestlers, ending the match early. Challenged the One-Winged Angel to a steel cage match at Rise to Power on 27 November 2004, then led the Pride to a win over Amity in the main event Bluff City Streetfight after new addition Derek Martin turned on the One-Winged Angel with a Pridebreaker for the pinfall. Fought Tigress to a double-disqualification draw for the UWF Meltdown Championship on 1 December 2004 after both wrestlers traded low blows and eye-rakes. On 11 December 2004, presented "Dead End" Derek Martin to the crowd as the Pride's own newest member, accepted a Ballbreaker Cage Match challenge from the One-Winged Angel, then interfered in Martin's own no-contest with Angel by chairshotting him off the top rope and joining the beatdown until Alex Kidd ran in. Won the UWF World Heavyweight Championship from Kyle Lee by pinfall (the Before the Fall piledriver) on 28 May 2005 under an Edmond Winston IV charter amendment naming him the automatic number-one contender, aided by Kari Stevens's interference, then blindsided Winston with a Pridebreaker after thanking him; introduced returning UWF original Brett Greene to the Pride beforehand and watched Greene turn on new recruit "Dead End" Derek Martin with a Brett Bomb. Celebrated his own UWF World Heavyweight Championship win on 11 June 2005 with confetti and streamers, framed it as three years of scheming against Edmond Winston IV, then accepted a rematch challenge from the One-Winged Angel for the following week. Introduced the Cornerstones as the Pride's own new tag team on 23 July 2005, then turned on longtime friend Brett Greene mid-main-event with a chair shot and a tandem Pridebreaker/the End combination, allowing Derek Martin to score the pin. Assigned Kari Stevens to mentor his debuting daughter Samantha on 3 August 2005; cut a Brawl From The Mall 6 promo on 6 August 2005 dismissing his own roster and warning Gold Rush challenger Alex Martinez, before UWF president Becky Byers banned the Pride and then every wrestler from ringside and named a special guest referee for the Gold Rush main event. Demanded his own rematch clause be honored on 18 March 2006, was denied an immediate World Heavyweight Championship shot by Becky Byers, and had his own microphone cut after arguing; booked instead for Luck of the Draw 2006.

tenures.note: A former UWF Cruiserweight and Rampage Champion, managed by Tesla St. James; pinned Alex Extreme with the Gone to Texas in a non-title one-on-one bout. Won the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship from Eugene Robinson with a Superfly Splash off the top of a steel cage on 25 October 2003, a stipulation Vice-President Jessica Marshall set specifically to hinder him. Retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship by disqualification against Randall Osbourne on 12 November 2003 after Osbourne repeatedly bit his forehead. Entered the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match, non-title; rolled up Alex Extreme for an elimination before Edmond Winston IV accidentally struck him in the face with a Diamond Dust meant for Michael Augustine, and Extreme later rolled him up for his own elimination. Jessica Marshall announced afterward that he must defend the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship in a gauntlet against Eugene Robinson, Tragedy, and Victor Frost at Eve of Destruction, after publicly accusing him of attacking President Sarah Reed. Broke up "Dead End" Derek Martin's backstage attack on Tesla St. James on 15 May 2004, agreeing to a Gold Rush street fight against him; teamed with Alex Kidd and Paul Wong against Team Canada and Scott Daniels in a six-man tag that ended without a decision amid a mass brawl, then helped carry an injured Wong to a hospital afterward. Interrupted Michael Augustine's own open-mic promo on 29 May 2004; after Vice-President Jessica Marshall offered him a place in the Gold Rush main event triple threat if he could beat Edmond Winston IV that same night, did exactly that by pinfall (Gone to Texas) with Augustine himself as special guest referee. "Dead End" Derek Martin blindsided him with the End immediately after the bell. Beat "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall (Gone to Texas) in a Gold Rush street fight on 5 June 2004, then won the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World later the same card, pinning champion Michael Augustine with a second Gone to Texas in a triple threat also involving Edmond Winston IV, after the real Alex Extreme exposed an impostor (Job Holly) who had been interfering on Winston's behalf. Escaped the cage first in a losing steel cage main event alongside Alex Kidd against the Hands of Death on 28 August 2004, but could not return in time to stop Serge Annis and Caliban's own Near Death Experience pin on Kidd; fell from a ladder set outside the cage after Annis took away his own steel chair. Retained the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World over Jamie Underwood by disqualification on 18 September 2004 after owner Edmond Winston IV struck him with a steel chair, then superplexed him from the top rope through a steel ladder propped against the ring apron. Returned from a long absence to team with Tesla St. James in a win over Alex Extreme and a substituting Nina Grimsson on 27 November 2004, pinning Extreme with the Gone To Texas; cut a pre-match promo vowing revenge on Edmond Winston IV ahead of their own Rise to Power ladder match for the World Heavyweight Championship. Retained the UWF World Heavyweight Championship over "The Last American Badass" Alex Martinez by pinfall (a surprise inside cradle) on 11 December 2004 in the main event, denying Martinez the title and, with it, Luke Kinsey's own shot at it for Rise to Power. Lost the UWF World Heavyweight Championship to Scott "Hotspot" Daniels by pinfall (the Before the Fall piledriver) on 28 May 2005, an impromptu title defense forced by an Edmond Winston IV charter amendment naming Daniels the automatic number-one contender after Rise to Power; Kari Stevens's own interference tipped the finish. Returned on 28 April 2007 as outside consultant to a newly-formed Metroplex Broadcast Consulting group, counseling Corey Irons on finding his own motivation and reuniting backstage with "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson; did not wrestle.

Beat Brian McKenzie by pinfall (Oblivion) and Paul Wong by disqualification to reach the UWF Meltdown Championship tournament finals on 8 September 2004, then fought Tigress to a twenty-minute time-limit draw. Lost to "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall (a hanging brainbuster suplex) on 6 October 2004, after briefly reversing the Dead End with a standing neck vice. Beat "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb by pinfall (Oblivion, a sacrifice-the-knee driver) on 3 November 2004, sacrificing an injured knee twice along the way to slow the newcomer down. Lost the UWF Cruiserweight Championship challenge to champion One-Winged Angel by disqualification on 11 June 2005 after working over the champion's own left leg for much of the match and refusing to break a rope-break hold. Won a Road to the Gold qualifier over Scorpio by referee stoppage on 22 June 2005 after three consecutive Oblivions left Scorpio unconscious, the Amazing Romanis pledging their support to him beforehand. Won his own match against Shadoe Rage by disqualification on 6 July 2005, sans manager Angel who was still recovering from an earlier beating, after Niklos and Ravnos Romani disguised themselves as duplicate Vyolynces to even the odds, then was chair-shotted and piledrivered by Shadoe once the Romanis were beaten off. Beat Jamie Underwood by pinfall (a piledriver) in a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round match on 3 August 2005 after Illuminati members Andrew "Flash" Tucker and L. Dan Dee interfered at ringside; earlier sat silently through a backstage conversation with Niklos Romani.

tenures.note: A silent, tattooed member of Sabbat Justice; teamed with Niklos and Ravnos Romani (the Arcana) in a six-man tag, won by disqualification when an opposing wrestler struck his own partner with a chair amid a locker-room prank. Failed to appear for the opening bell of a billed tag match on 22 October 2003, then arrived mid-beatdown to chokeslam Alex Extreme through the ringside table; no decision was ever rendered. Won a one-on-one match with Alex Kidd by disqualification on 12 November 2003 after Alex Extreme and the Sons of Cacaphony ran in three-on-one; fought the trio off until Rodney used a cattle prod on him. Eliminated from the 17 December 2003 battle royal when the ropes gave way under his own weight during a Cameron Black onslaught.
