tenures.note: The UWF's own co-owner; personally wrestled protege Jamie Underwood on 24 March 2004 after first offering him a staged win, turning on him for real once Underwood accepted it. The match ended without a decision when Sabbath, then Michael Augustine and Alex Extreme, then the Privateers all ran in in succession; Winston set up a handicap main event, the Youngbloods against his own New Era, for the following Rampage. Teamed with Underwood and the Privateers against Michael Augustine and Alex Extreme in that own handicap main event on 15 May 2004; the Privateers turned on him mid-match to side with Extreme, triple-conchairtoing him and putting him through a table before Augustine turned on Extreme in turn. Delivered a chess-themed office monologue on 19 May 2004 naming Serge Annis and Caliban as the instrument of his revenge on the Privateers; does not compete on this card. Lost the main event to Kyle Lee by pinfall on 29 May 2004 with World Champion Michael Augustine as special guest referee, putting Lee into the Gold Rush main event triple threat against Winston and Augustine for the World Heavyweight Championship. Competed in the Gold Rush main event triple threat for the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World on 5 June 2004, losing when Kyle Lee pinned champion Michael Augustine after the real Alex Extreme knocked out both Winston and Augustine, exposing an impostor Alex Extreme (Job Holly) who had been assisting Winston. Escaped a Tower of Doom cage match last on 30 October 2004, and only after being hurled bodily out of the top cage's own door by Alex Martinez; his team (with Victor Frost, Papa Legba, and Luke Kinsey) was declared the winner once he landed outside the structure, though he was left unconscious and bleeding, then beaten further by a surprise-returning "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee and by all four opponents after the bell. Beat Alex Kidd in a Tuxedo Death Match on 13 November 2004 after Kidd failed to answer referee Ingraham's ten count following a cobra clutch suplex, in a brawl that spilled from the ring to his own limousine; dragged to safety afterward by a returning Scott Daniels and Team Canada before Kyle Lee and other fan favorites could reach him. Warned Jamie Underwood backstage on 27 November 2004 that Sabbath would beat him badly at Rise to Power, then agreed to face Sabbath himself the following week in a Hardcore Match to prepare Underwood; sparred with new signing Luke Kinsey over Marshall Law's own unpopularity. Lost a self-arranged Hardcore Rules match to Sabbath by pinfall (a Black Tie Suplex through a table) on 11 December 2004, a brutal contest that also put both men through a pane of glass and a section of hockey boards; watched Luke Kinsey's own world title opportunity develop from his own skybox during the main event.

N.E.W.'s rich young newcomer, whose family's Winston Tobacco offered the federation a sizeable grant: billed in the Rising Star Championship match of 12 November 2000 in his second professional match, was billed against Mad Goat a week later, arrived by limousine at Slam Dance II, and was billed to defend the Rising Star Championship against Victor V. Hill on 3 December 2000. The same Big Tobacco heel and limousine entrance as the UWF's co-owner of 2003-2004.

tenures.note: Billed from Austin, Texas, a fellow MBC wrestler of champion Paul Wong; pinned Wong with a top-rope moonsault elbowdrop (Hell's Halo) to win the UWF Rampage Championship. Retained the title against Simon O'Neal on 25 October 2003, reversing a corner whip into a body splash and flowing into a roll-up for the pin; his own tag team stablemates Rage and Spice, together billed as Fury, debuted the same night. Retained the UWF Rampage Championship again on 15 November 2003, hitting a top-rope moonsault elbowdrop (Hell's Halo) on Brian McKenzie after manager Virginia St. Ursula distracted McKenzie with a bottle of Bailey's Irish Cream. Retained the UWF Rampage Championship again on 20 December 2003, pinning Scott "Hotspot" Daniels with the Revelator after Quinn Brown's own entrance music distracted Daniels moments after he had knocked out the referee. By 24 March 2004 the title was billed on a different wrestler, Uriah Hawkins; no surviving document in the held record states the match, date, or method by which the reign changed hands. Won a four corners contenders match on 19 May 2004 over Chris O'Brien, T.D. Swagger, and November, lifting Swagger into a Revelator and driving him down across the other two fallen men for the pin, earning a UWF Cruiserweight Championship match against Michael Bonn at Gold Rush. Won the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World from Michael Bonn by pinfall at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, reversing Bonn's own Deadfall into an uranage before finishing with a top-rope Hell's Halo, after cornerwoman Ami Tran and Amity stablemate Spice each ran interference at ringside. Retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over Michael Bonn by pinfall on 28 August 2004, catching a top-rope hurricanrana attempt and turning it into the Revelator for the pin. Retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over Chris O'Brien on 22 September 2004, a friendly contest between MBC friends that ended with the Heavenly Wind and Hell's Halo combination, cornerwoman Ami Tran dubbing it "Divine Intervention." Beat "Agony" Michael Augustine by disqualification in a non-title match on 30 October 2004 after Erik Grimsson pulled Augustine off the top rope to stop a chair-assisted diving attack; a mass brawl followed involving the Privateers and manager Allison Ivey, leaving Angel busted open. Led Amity (Rage, Spice) into the Bluff City Streetfight main event against the Pride on 27 November 2004, nearly winning with a cane-assisted DDT before Derek Martin turned on him mid-match, chairshotting him and hitting a Pridebreaker for the loss. Watched from the Fury locker room as Rage and Spice prepared for their own losing UWF World Tag Team Championship challenge on 1 December 2004, promising to "Harlequinize" Derek Martin. On 11 December 2004, fought Martin to a no-contest in a match that broke down after the referee was knocked out, hitting a Heavenly Wind Hurricanrana before Scott Daniels's own chairshot ended the contest as pure chaos; saved from a Pridebreaker by a returning Alex Kidd. Retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over Youth Gone Wild by pinfall (a top-rope german release suplex) on 25 May 2005 in a hard-fought, mutually respectful contest, then launched Amity's own "I'm Rich, Bitch" North American tour with Rage and Spice. Challenged World Champion Scott Daniels to a rematch on 11 June 2005 and had it accepted for the following week, then retained the UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World over Vyolynce by disqualification after Vyolynce refused to break a leg hold at the ropes. Arrived at Madison Square Garden with fellow Amity members on 28 April 2007 billed as the newly-crowned UWF Cruiserweight Champion of the World, then interrupted Luke Kinsey's own hasty exit after Kinsey's title defense to declare himself the next challenger for the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World.

name: Rage
caption: One-half of Fury, the One-Winged Angel's Amity tag team stablemates, debuting with a win over the Universal Powers.

tenures.note: Teamed with Spice as Fury, part of the One-Winged Angel's Amity faction; scored a pinfall win over the Universal Powers' Todd Franklin with the Motor City Massacre in their debut. Teamed with Spice as Fury again on 21 March 2004 in a losing effort against Serge Annis and Caliban, caught by a Caliban superplex across Annis's own outstretched knee for the pinfall. Teamed with Spice and newly-arrived Amity member Ami Tran to beat Team Canada (Trevor Hextall, Bob Jablonski) and Kari Stevens by pinfall on 6 October 2004, Tran finishing Stevens with a version of the One-Winged Angel's own Revelator. Teamed with Spice and the One-Winged Angel as Amity in a losing Bluff City Streetfight main event against the Pride on 27 November 2004, backdropped through a technician's table by Team Canada before Derek Martin's own surprise heel turn decided the match. Lost the UWF World Tag Team Championship challenge with Spice against the Privateers by pinfall on 1 December 2004, mocked by "Supervixen" Ami Tran beforehand for Amity's own flat mood since losing a streetfight to the Pride. On 11 December 2004, brawled backstage with Trevor Hextall in a Pride-Fury melee that spilled through the arena. Traded threats backstage with the Privateers on 28 May 2005 over the Youngbloods' own history with Lisa Drake, then interfered at ringside during the Privateers' own losing UWF World Tag Team Championship rematch against the Sons of Cacophony. Lost to Strictly Business by pinfall on 8 June 2005 after tag partner Spice was driven onto a steel chair, then was jumped by the Privateers immediately afterward alongside Spice. Advanced in a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005 when Ravnos Romani failed to appear, backed at ringside by tag partner Spice and Ami Tran. Arrived at Madison Square Garden with fellow Amity members Ami Tran, Spice, and the One-Winged Angel on 28 April 2007; did not wrestle.

identity.note: An unrelated RSPWF Top 200 stub of the identical ring name is tagged to different federations (WeW, HCW, IWF) in a different year; nothing links the two beyond the bare name.

name: Spice
caption: One-half of Fury, the One-Winged Angel's Amity tag team stablemates, debuting with a win over the Universal Powers.

tenures.note: Teamed with Rage as Fury, part of the One-Winged Angel's Amity faction, in a debut win over the Universal Powers. Teamed with Rage as Fury again on 21 March 2004 in a losing effort against Serge Annis and Caliban, absorbing a pumphandle slam across the ringsteps before the finish. Teamed with Rage and newly-arrived Amity member Ami Tran to beat Team Canada (Trevor Hextall, Bob Jablonski) and Kari Stevens by pinfall on 6 October 2004, setting up the finish with a benchpress toss of Stevens across Tran's own outstretched knee. Teamed with Rage and the One-Winged Angel as Amity in a losing Bluff City Streetfight main event against the Pride on 27 November 2004, brawling up the entrance stage with Team Canada and taking a double DDT before Derek Martin's own surprise heel turn decided the match. Lost the UWF World Tag Team Championship challenge with Rage against the Privateers by pinfall on 1 December 2004, complaining loudly about Amity's own losing streak beforehand. On 11 December 2004, brawled backstage with Bob Jablonski in a Pride-Fury melee that spilled through the arena. Traded threats backstage with the Privateers on 28 May 2005 over the Youngbloods' own history with Lisa Drake, then interfered at ringside during the Privateers' own losing UWF World Tag Team Championship rematch against the Sons of Cacophony. Was pinned by Strictly Business's Bad Credit DDT onto a steel chair on 8 June 2005, then was jumped by the Privateers alongside tag partner Rage immediately afterward. Backed Rage at ringside for a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005. Arrived at Madison Square Garden with fellow Amity members Ami Tran, Rage, and the One-Winged Angel on 28 April 2007; did not wrestle.

name: Bobby Lincoln
caption: One-half of the Universal Powers, signed by Vice-President Jessica Marshall and sent after the Keenings, the Fraternity Boys, and Youth Gone Wild.

tenures.note: Teamed with brother Todd Franklin as the Universal Powers; lost their debut tag match to Fury (Rage and Spice). Teamed with Todd Franklin as the Universal Powers again on 17 December 2003, unable to stop Niklos Romani's forearm from breaking up his own cover in a loss to the Arcana. Teamed with Todd Franklin as the Universal Powers again on 21 March 2004, pinned by the Sons of Cacaphony's Sky Hammer combination in a losing UWF North American Tag Team Championship challenge. Teamed with Todd Franklin as the Universal Powers again on 19 May 2004, beating the Harlequins after Niklos Romani's own pre-match chair ambush and an unidentified interloper's interference. Won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with Todd Franklin from the Sons of Cacaphony on 28 August 2004 in a street fight after an unidentified masked interloper knocked Erik Grimsson out from inside a locker-room closet, clearing the way for Franklin's own pinfall. Lost alongside Todd Franklin and Randall Osbourne to the Sons of Cacaphony and Alex Martinez on 22 September 2004, Franklin pinned by a version of the Harlequins' own Reality Check from Martinez and Erik Grimsson. Lost the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with Todd Franklin to the Amazing Romanis (Niklos and Ravnos Romani) by pinfall on 20 October 2004, pinned by a Niklos Romani neckbreaker delivered off his own brother's shoulders, after a returning Vyolynce's own ringside chair distraction.

name: Todd Franklin
caption: One-half of the Universal Powers, signed by Vice-President Jessica Marshall and sent after the Keenings, the Fraternity Boys, and Youth Gone Wild.

tenures.note: Teamed with brother Bobby Lincoln as the Universal Powers; pinned by Fury's Motor City Massacre in their debut tag match. Teamed with Bobby Lincoln as the Universal Powers again on 17 December 2003, pinned by Ravnos Romani's small package in a loss to the Arcana. Teamed with Bobby Lincoln as the Universal Powers again on 21 March 2004, challenging the Sons of Cacaphony for the UWF North American Tag Team Championship in a losing effort that ended when both teams traded dives to the floor. Forced into a scrambled-partners tag with a reluctant Niklos Romani on 5 May 2004; turned on his own partner mid-match, chokeslamming and lariating him before finishing Erik Grimsson with a New Horizon Line, ending the bout as a no-contest and declaring the Universal Powers done being overlooked. Teamed with Bobby Lincoln as the Universal Powers again on 19 May 2004, beating the Harlequins after Niklos Romani's own pre-match chair ambush and an unidentified interloper's interference; finished Terror with the Universal Elimination. Won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with Bobby Lincoln from the Sons of Cacaphony on 28 August 2004 in a street fight, finishing a knocked-out Erik Grimsson with a superkick for the pin after an unidentified masked interloper ambushed him from inside a locker-room closet. Lost a mismatched partners tag match alongside Jacob Drake to Ravnos Romani and a substituting Alex Extreme by pinfall on 18 September 2004, blinded by the Gypsy Curse powder before Romani's brass-knuckled rollup. Lost alongside Bobby Lincoln and Randall Osbourne to the Sons of Cacaphony and Alex Martinez on 22 September 2004, pinned by a version of the Harlequins' own Reality Check from Martinez and Erik Grimsson. Lost the UWF North American Tag Team Championship alongside Bobby Lincoln to the Amazing Romanis (Niklos and Ravnos Romani) by pinfall on 20 October 2004, flattened by the Romanis' own Total Elimination combination before Niklos pinned Lincoln for the title change, aided by a returning Vyolynce's own ringside chair distraction.

name: Comedy
caption: A Harlequin-styled wrestler who teamed with the Love Sisters against the Coven, and who claims a history with Leanna Love from a prior title switch in the MBC.

tenures.note: Teamed with the Love Sisters against the Coven, cleared from the ring by Angel's machine-gun knees before Leanna Love was pinned. Leanna Love's own pre-match remarks describe Comedy tricking her out of a title in the MBC years earlier; no MBC document in the held record corroborates that history. Teamed with Melody in a losing four corners women's tag war on 25 August 2004 against the debuting Team BATTLE*DREAM (Reona Yoshida and Misaki Ishikawa), the Love Sisters, and Extreme Measures (Lisa Drake and Nina Grimsson).

name: Pierce Bleed
caption: The unhinged half of the tag team Happy Hardcore, pinned by Victor Frost's top-rope superbomb in a non-title singles match.

tenures.note: Billed from Hell's Kitchen, New York, weighing 284 pounds, one-half of Happy Hardcore; pulled Victor Frost back from a crowd confrontation mid-match before losing by pinfall to a top-rope superbomb. Returned to the active roster on 5 May 2004 off the suspended list, ranting to partner T.D. Swagger about the team's own bad luck; lost by pinfall to November's tornado DDT, then threw the UWF Meltdown Championship belt into the crowd during the main event and firebombed Edmond Winston IV's limousine afterward. Challenged Uriah Hawkins for the UWF Rampage Championship at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004 in a title-versus-contract match, using a cordless microphone to knock out the champion and take a countable pinfall; special referee T.D. Swagger overturned the finish and restarted the bout, in which Hawkins pinned him with a Suicide DDT, voiding his own UWF contract under the match's own stipulation.

name: Tigress
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2001: #83, tagged UWF; 2004: #169, tagged UWF. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Held a place in the RSPWF Top 200 for two editions running, highest at #83 in 2001 and lowest at #169 in 2004.

tenures.note: Teamed with Leslie Hernandez and Angel as the Coven in a win over the Love Sisters and Comedy, stomping and taunting Comedy before tagging out. Reached the semi-finals of the 17 December 2003 Meltdown Championship tournament, surviving the battle royal, before Paul Wong caught her in midair off a Tiger Pounce attempt and drilled her with a Samoan drop for the pin. Beat "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict by pinfall on 10 March 2004 with a double Sumatran Headhunter, then interfered in Papa Legba's own Meltdown Championship defense against Alex Kidd later the same card; announced afterward, over drinks with Papa Legba, that she was splitting from Sabbat Justice to go independent. Ate takeout with her pet tiger Harley while discussing an upcoming match with Simon O'Neal and Donna Tetreault, then teamed with Papa Legba on 19 May 2004 to beat O'Neal and Tetreault for the UWF Meltdown Championship, using a handful of powder to blind the referee before Legba's top-rope splash finished it. Beat Scorpio by pinfall (the Poacher's Woe) and advanced to the UWF Meltdown Championship tournament finals on a bye after Papa Legba and Uriah Hawkins fought to a double countout, then fought Vyolynce to a twenty-minute time-limit draw. Won the UWF Meltdown Championship from Collision Holly by submission (the Marjara Mallaka) on 22 September 2004, sitting her full weight across Holly's legs until he tapped, after Vyolynce declined to compete in the advertised three-way and left the ring before the bell. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Youth Gone Wild by submission with an inverted dragon sleeper on 6 October 2004, accepting the challenger's own post-match handshake to a large ovation. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Bobby Nash by pinfall (the Sumatran Headhunter, using the ropes for leverage) on 20 October 2004, despite giving up a large size disadvantage. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn by disqualification on 3 November 2004, after a six-wrestler UWF tryout group (revealed to be led by a disguised T.D. Swagger) ran in and beat Bonn down. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Scorpio by submission (the Marjara Mallaka) on 17 November 2004. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Scott "Hotspot" Daniels in a draw on 1 December 2004 after both wrestlers were disqualified for a simultaneous low blow and eye-rake, an ugly title defense that began with Tigress blasting Daniels with the belt before the bell. Fought Marissa Monet to a double disqualification for the UWF Meltdown Championship on 25 May 2005 after both wrestlers shoved the referee, ending an ugly grudge match that began with a promo in which Tigress gutted a shark on camera to make her point. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Marissa Monet by submission (a modified Marjara Mallaka surfboard) in a No DQ rematch on 8 June 2005, after telling reporter Debbie Henshall she would rather have lost cleanly than share another double disqualification; President Becky Byers announced afterward that the defense was the Meltdown Championship's own last, with the title to be unified with the Rampage Championship the following week. Lost the UWF Meltdown Championship to Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit by pinfall (the 51st Drop) in a title unification match on 22 June 2005, ending the Meltdown Championship's own separate history; needled Nuit backstage beforehand over his own sentimentality about the belt. Rebuffed an awkward backstage approach from John DeWolfe about a possible Bod Squad partnership on 20 July 2005, while sharpening a katana in her own locker room. Challenged Marcus Nuit for the Unified Television Championship at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, losing by pinfall after a tense top-rope exchange; signed autographs for fans backstage beforehand. Teamed with Luke Kinsey in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, submitting a debuting Samantha Daniels with a double armbar rollup before being catapulted over the top rope by Jason Keening.

name: Youth Gone Wild
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1998: #176, tagged UWF, EMWC; 1999: #27, tagged UWF, EMWC; 2003: #185, tagged UWF. caption: Placed in three editions of the RSPWF Top 200 — #176 in 1998, #27 in 1999, #185 in 2003 — best at #27.

tenures.note: Teamed with Alex Kidd, Paul Wong, and Quinn Brown to a count-out win over the Pride, hitting a double elbowdrop with Kidd early in the match. Teamed with Eugene Robinson in a non-title losing effort against UWF World Tag Team Champions Team Canada on 12 November 2003. Answered Serge Annis's open challenge on 15 November 2003 after Cameron Black refused to appear, busting Annis open with a top-rope DDT reversal before losing to an Epitomizer chokeslam. Entered the 17 December 2003 battle royal; his own elimination went unannounced by name. Lost his own in-ring debut opponent's debut on 10 March 2004, pinned by "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker's Planting Flowers for the Dead after a top-rope elbow strike. Lost a UWF Meltdown Championship challenge to champion Tigress by submission (an inverted dragon sleeper) on 6 October 2004, extending a handshake to the champion afterward. Lost a UWF Cruiserweight Championship challenge to One-Winged Angel by pinfall (a top-rope german release suplex) on 25 May 2005 after a near-fall of his own on a Revelator-style counter. Lost a Road to the Gold qualifier to L. Dan Dee by submission on 22 June 2005. Beat "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn in the Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament's own first round on 6 July 2005 with a top-rope Wildflyer moonsault, in a hard-fought, mutually respectful contest. Made a surprise return on 3 August 2005 to save Alex Martinez from a Cornerstones beatdown, only to be low-blowed and piledriven by Daniel Kidd afterward; recorded a backstage promo on 6 August 2005 telling Kidd he now remembered how personal the business could get.

name: Fantasy Girl
caption: A masked debutante who defeated Mitzi Sukkora with a top-rope moonsault press, her identity never revealed on this broadcast.

tenures.note: A masked, high-flying wrestler billed only as Fantasy Girl; pinned "Mystical" Mitzi Sukkora with a top-rope moonsault press in her in-ring debut. Her identity behind the mask was not revealed. Lost an interpromotional attraction match to "Battle Princess" Misaki Ishikawa of Project BATTLE*DREAM on 19 May 2004, pinned by a Skull Crash Buster after a back-and-forth contest. Returned from a tour of Japan carrying the Beauty Angels: Japan Skyweight Championship and beat debuting Samantha Daniels by pinfall (the Fantasy Bomb) on 3 August 2005.

name: "Mystical" Mitzi Sukkora
caption: A debuting wrestler who lost her own debut match to the masked Fantasy Girl by pinfall.

tenures.note: Entered to Tomoyasu Hotei's "Battle Without Honor or Humanity"; lost her debut match to the masked Fantasy Girl by pinfall (top-rope moonsault press) after trading several near-falls. Lost to Kari Stevens by pinfall (corkscrew 450 splash) on 5 May 2004 in Stevens's own forced-through in-ring debut. Was pinned by Amazing Grace's own 450 splash in a four-way singles debut match for Grace on 8 June 2005, also involving "All Night" Wendy Minow and "Long Haul" Greg Embrey.

name: Collision Holly
caption: A debuting wrestler representing the Heroes of Sports Entertainment, knocked out cold by a single Cameron Black right hand in his own debut match.

tenures.note: Billed representing the Heroes of Sports Entertainment; knocked unconscious by a single right hand from a freshly-ambushed Cameron Black before either man could properly start the match. Lost to debuting Brazilian cruiserweight Scorpio by pinfall (a top-rope frog splash) on 5 May 2004. Won the UWF Meltdown Championship from Papa Legba by pinfall on 25 August 2004, catching the champion with a second-rope bulldog after a long beating. Lost the UWF Meltdown Championship to Tigress by submission (the Marjara Mallaka) on 22 September 2004 after Vyolynce, the match's own advertised third man, declined to compete and left the ring before the bell. Lost alongside Job Holly to the Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) by pinfall on 3 November 2004, blinded by Shadoe Rage's own cape for an opening lariat before Job Holly took the Apocalypse combination for the finish.

tenures.note: Billed from Northwest Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, leader of the Youngbloods, accompanied by Allison Ivey; entered the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match, pinning Edward Drake with the Path of Bones nervehold and Chad Grimsson with an Impact DDT before being counted out alongside Edmond Winston IV after the two brawled out of the arena. Vice-President Jessica Marshall announced afterward that he would challenge Winston for the UWF World Heavyweight Championship at Eve of Destruction. Teamed with Alex Extreme against Edmond Winston IV, Jamie Underwood, and the Privateers on 15 May 2004; after the Privateers turned on Winston to side with Extreme, Augustine turned on Extreme in turn, joining the Privateers to beat him through two tables before Alex Martinez and the Sons of Cacaphony ran in. Announced with Allison Ivey on 19 May 2004 that he and the Privateers had purchased minority shares of the UWF; does not compete on this card. Lost the UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World to Kyle Lee by pinfall in the Gold Rush main event triple threat on 5 June 2004, also involving Edmond Winston IV, pinned by a second Gone to Texas after the real Alex Extreme exposed an impostor (Job Holly) who had been interfering on Winston's behalf. His "Singles War" against Alex Martinez was never brought under control and ended without a decision on 18 September 2004 after the Privateers and a returning Alex Extreme turned the brawl into a four-man fight; manager Allison Ivey struck Martinez with a high kick during the match. Lost a non-title match to the One-Winged Angel by disqualification on 30 October 2004 after Erik Grimsson pulled him off the top rope to stop a chair-assisted diving attack; joined manager Allison Ivey and the Privateers in a post-match beatdown of Grimsson and Angel. Fought Scott "Hotspot" Daniels to a no-contest on 3 November 2004 after Kari Stevens and Allison Ivey both struck their own man's opponent with a chair and Amity ran in on both wrestlers, ending the match early. Challenged Alex Extreme to a match at Rise to Power on 27 November 2004, then looked on as Jacob Drake and Allison Ivey beat down Lisa Drake for refusing to rejoin the Youngbloods, restrained from joining in by Allison Ivey herself. Mocked the Illuminati and the new World champion for overlooking the Youngbloods on 8 June 2005, then lost a UWF North American Heavyweight Championship match to champion Papa Legba by pinfall (the Ragga Bomb); called out Legba for a grudge fight on 11 June 2005, naming him one of only two men to ever truly beat him. Beat Jason Keening with a cradle brainbuster in a random-partners tag match alongside Victor Frost against Keening and Miguel Quesada on 23 July 2005, then called out and accepted a Gold Rush title challenge from North American Heavyweight Champion Papa Legba. Eliminated fifth from the main event eight-man elimination match on 3 August 2005, pinned by Sabbath's Spinning Sabby Driver after himself eliminating Papa Legba.

name: "Swinger" Troy Grace
caption: A cocky North Carolina debutante who beat Job Holly and T.D. Swagger by relying more on cheating than his own natural talent.

tenures.note: Entered to "Hate To Say I Told You So" by the Hives; beat Job Holly in his own debut by submission (Saving Grace, a Sasorigatame) after using illegal leverage off the ropes. Beat "Jukebox" T.D. Swagger on 21 March 2004 by pinfall (Ace Crusher), again relying on eye rakes and a knife-edge chop to the throat along the way. Challenged Uriah Hawkins for the UWF Rampage Championship on 15 May 2004 in a three-way dance also involving Quinn Brown, losing when Hawkins caught both men together with a double DDT for the pin.

name: Job Holly
caption: A debuting wrestler thoroughly outclassed and submitted by "Swinger" Troy Grace in his own debut match.

tenures.note: Entered to "The Art Of Losing" by American Hi-Fi to a surprisingly loud pop; comprehensively beaten down by "Swinger" Troy Grace before submitting to the Saving Grace (Sasorigatame) in his own in-ring debut. Beaten by debuting rookie Marcus Nuit on 22 September 2004, finished with a running Lyger Bomb after a flurry of quick offense. Lost alongside Collision Holly to the Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) by pinfall on 3 November 2004, finished with the Prophets' own Apocalypse combination.

name: "Prairie Fire" Mark Marleau
caption: A Saskatoon debutante who beat Taurus with the Saskatoon Special in front of a hometown-adjacent Edmonton crowd.

tenures.note: Entered to Audioslave's "Show Me How To Live"; billed from Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, and introduced himself as a same-day replacement summoned by Commissioner Becky Byers. Beat Taurus in his own in-ring debut by pinfall with the Saskatoon Special (a roundhouse kick) after a late bearhug rally by his opponent. Lost to "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker by pinfall on 5 May 2004, knocked out by an uppercut after Parker methodically worked over his knee.

name: Taurus
caption: A member of the Heroes of Sports Entertainment, pinned by "Prairie Fire" Mark Marleau's Saskatoon Special in his own in-ring debut.

tenures.note: Billed representing the Heroes of Sports Entertainment alongside Collision Holly; lost his own in-ring debut to "Prairie Fire" Mark Marleau by pinfall (the Saskatoon Special) after a late bearhug rally. Lost to a returning Steve Ryott by pinfall (a top-rope Ryott Bomb) on 25 August 2004 after taking an inverted DDT. Lost his UWF debut-tournament opener to "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas by submission (the End of the Show cobra clutch) on 8 September 2004. Beat Simon O'Neal by pinfall on 6 October 2004 after O'Neal collapsed attempting a bodyslam, an upset that stunned the crowd into silence. Lost to debuting "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb by pinfall (the Atom Smasher, a double underhook piledriver) on 20 October 2004.

name: "Alluring" Arielle Starr
caption: A high-flying regular of the Sun Belt Angels who lost to Donna Tetreault by upset pinfall, then teamed with Tesla St. James and Fantasy Girl in a losing effort against the Misfits.

tenures.note: Normally teams as one of the Sun Belt Angels; lost to Donna Tetreault by pinfall (Domination Day suplex) on 10 March 2004 after Myra Benedict's ringside knife distracted her from a Starrstruck attempt. Teamed with Tesla St. James and Fantasy Girl on 21 March 2004 in a losing six-woman tag against the Misfits (Marissa Monet, Sierra Browne, and Dalbello Rage), describing the match beforehand as payback for years of run-ins with all three. Lost to Alicia Powers on 19 May 2004 in Powers's own singles debut, her leg buckling mid-suplex and leaving her open to a Michinoku Driver; myra Benedict threw a knife into her dressing-room door earlier that night. Beat Myra Benedict by pinfall at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, countering a second Shadow's Bane kick with the Bedazzler enzuigiri before finishing with a top-rope Skytwister Press. A UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World challenge against champion Donna Tetreault on 13 November 2004 ended without a finish after Sierra Browne, Alicia Powers and "Tornado" Tara Smith ran in on Tetreault's behalf; Starr was struck by a chain-loaded glove shot meant for the fleeing champion. Lost a UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship challenge to Sierra Browne by pinfall (a top-rope moonsault) on 28 May 2005. Ran down to help clear the ring of the Bod Squad during the Wind Walkers' own women's tag match on 20 July 2005. Confronted Kari Stevens backstage over an attack on Stephanie Harper on 3 August 2005, was blindsided by Amazing Grace, and was saved by Leslie Hernandez, the two agreeing to team against Stevens and Grace at Gold Rush.

name: "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict
caption: Poison Bliss Myra Benedict's cousin and Chad Grimsson's girlfriend, pinned by a double Sumatran Headhunter from Tigress after her own relationship with Grimsson fell apart on camera.

tenures.note: Entered to Death by Stereo's "Getting It Off My Chest"; broke up with boyfriend Chad Grimsson backstage beforehand over his interference in her earlier Eve of Destruction match against Myra Benedict, her own cousin. Lost to Tigress by pinfall (a double Sumatran Headhunter) after her attention split between the match and the entrance ramp. Ambushed Nina Grimsson backstage on 24 March 2004 with a chair, then beat her by disqualification on 5 May 2004 with a fluorescent light tube, fleeing before Tesla St. James and Lisa Drake could reach the ring; began a relationship with Jamie Underwood the same night. Traded threats backstage with ex-boyfriend Chad Grimsson on 19 May 2004, then won by disqualification over Lisa Drake after Nina Grimsson and Tesla St. James beat her unconscious with Drake's own Singapore cane; interfered from ringside afterward to hold Grimsson's leg down for Jamie Underwood's own pinfall win over him. Returned from suspension on 28 May 2005 after Sabbath's own stipulation at Rise to Power lifted it, revealing that her feud with boyfriend Chad Grimsson, her staged romance with Jamie Underwood, and her attacks on Nina Grimsson had all been an elaborate scheme against Edmond Winston IV and Jessica Marshall; was confronted afterward by a mysterious figure known only as Angel over her own family's history. Met a returning "War Machine" Corey Irons and his companion Exotica in a parking lot on 8 June 2005, discussing her own recent confrontation with Angel and her family's motorcycle-riding sister, Ronnie; caught up with "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson backstage on 11 June 2005 over drinks, recapping the elaborate scheme the two had run against Edmond Winston IV and Jessica Marshall and agreeing to stay alert for further moves from Angel. Denied to reporter Moe Owens on 6 July 2005 that she attacked Angel with a pipe, promising consequences for Angel's own accusation. Accused by Angel of trying to run her down with a motorcycle backstage on 20 July 2005; sent to police custody alongside Angel by Becky Byers and forfeited her own scheduled return match against Naomi Ishikawa as a result. Asked "War Machine" Corey Irons on 23 July 2005 to watch over her against the Hands of Death, and attacked Angel in the aisle after her Women's Heavyweight Championship match that same night. Fought Angel and the Kindred to a no-contest alongside Leanna Love on 6 August 2005, knocking out cousin Myra Benedict with a steel chair before chasing Angel to the back. Teamed with Corey Irons in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, eliminated over the top by Moira Faith after agreeing to compete as a favor to Irons despite her own focus on an upcoming I Quit match with Angel. Won that I Quit match on 18 March 2006 by referee stoppage after a Burning Sunset Flip sent Angel head-first to the arena floor, using a steel chair, a lead pipe, and repeated headbutts throughout a brutal contest; was confronted backstage afterward by a taunting Angst.

name: "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker
caption: A Texan debutante who upset Youth Gone Wild in his own in-ring debut before losing his following week to Michael Keening.

tenures.note: Billed from Quintana, Texas; beat Youth Gone Wild in his own in-ring debut by pinfall with Planting Flowers for the Dead, a super implant DDT, after the two traded near-falls. Lost to "Banshee" Michael Keening on 21 March 2004, caught by a top-rope somersault splash after a Twisting Monster Drop had put both men down. Beat "Prairie Fire" Mark Marleau by pinfall on 5 May 2004, working over his opponent's knee before knocking him out with an uppercut, then cut a menacing pre-taped promo aimed at Marleau ahead of their match. Dismissed "Dead End" Derek Martin as a corporate sellout in a pre-match promo, then lost to him by pinfall on 19 May 2004, caught with an inverted ace crusher after ducking a straight punch.

name: Brianna Landis
caption: Tara Marshall's teenage personal assistant and sister-in-law, beaten by referee stoppage in her own first match against "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict.

tenures.note: The Women's Tag Team Co-Champion Tara Marshall's personal assistant and sister-in-law; ambushed "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict at Marshall's own instruction in place of a scheduled Bod Squad opponent, and lost by referee stoppage after Benedict locked on a DDT-and-leg-scissors chokehold. Lost to Alicia Powers by pinfall (a Michinoku Driver) on 25 August 2004; joined Tara Marshall's post-match beatdown of Powers until Tara Smith ran in to chase the Bod Squad off. Retained the UWF Women's Tag Team Championship with tag partner Tara "Sunburst" Marshall over Team BATTLE*DREAM by disqualification on 8 September 2004, surviving a near-finish spike piledriver before Marshall's interference. Lost a UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship challenge to champion Donna Tetreault by pinfall (the Dominion Day windmill suplex) on 18 September 2004 after tag partner Tara "Sunburst" Marshall knocked her from the top turnbuckle with a belt shot. Lost a non-title six-woman tag alongside Tara "Sunburst" Marshall and a late-arriving Donna Tetreault to Sierra Browne and Team BATTLE*DREAM on 2 October 2004, finished by Sierra Browne's own Truth Superkick. Knocked unconscious in a women's three-way dance on 20 October 2004 attempting a top-rope tornado DDT on Tara Smith, who ducked clear; Smith and Reona Yoshida each locked on a separate submission hold afterward and were both declared winners. Backed up tag partner Tara Marshall in a backstage confrontation with Commissioner Becky Byers on 27 November 2004, only for Byers to announce a UWF Women's Tag Team Championship defense against Team BATTLE*DREAM ("Tornado" Tara Smith, Alicia Powers) at Rise to Power. Beat Reona Yoshida by pinfall (a high moonsault press) on 1 December 2004 after tag partner Tara "Sunburst" Marshall knocked Misaki Ishikawa out at ringside with the Bod Squad's own title belt, drawing Yoshida briefly from the ring. Lost with tag partner Tara "Sunburst" Marshall to "Tornado" Tara Smith and Alicia Powers by pinfall (a 450 splash) on 25 May 2005 after nearly finishing Powers herself with a fireman's-carry frog splash. Joined Tara "Sunburst" Marshall in ambushing Lisa Drake from behind at John DeWolfe's direction on 8 June 2005, then broke up Alicia Powers and "Tornado" Tara Smith's own match against Drake and Leslie Hernandez, ending it as a no contest. Accompanied John DeWolfe and Tara Marshall to the ring on 22 June 2005, kissed on camera by DeWolfe before the trio was run off by Lisa Drake, Alicia Powers, and "Tornado" Tara Smith. Interfered twice in Tara Marshall's own loss to Alicia Powers on 6 July 2005, breaking up pin attempts before the match was thrown out. Pulled Alicia Powers off the ring apron during the Wind Walkers' own women's tag match on 20 July 2005 as part of a Bod Squad run-in that led to a no-decision. Learned partner John DeWolfe had not gotten the Bod Squad out of their Brawl From The Mall match on 3 August 2005; handed DeWolfe the ring bell to finish Lisa Drake for the win in that six-person tag on 6 August 2005. Revealed on 7 June 2006 to have been wrestling as the masked Fantasy Girl, unmasking after pinning sister-in-law Tara Marshall and attacking her further with a top-rope double moonsault kneedrop, an apron-to-floor Death Valley Driver, and a 450 splash onto her stretcher; husband Tom Landis pulled her away as EMTs moved Marshall. Carried husband Luke Kinsey's own UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World belt to ringside for his title defense against "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn on 28 April 2007, mocking challenger Bonn beforehand as an unworthy opponent; the match ended in a double countout.

name: "Jukebox" T.D. Swagger
caption: One half of Happy Hardcore, pinned by "Swinger" Troy Grace's Ace Crusher after issuing an open challenge on Winston's behalf.

tenures.note: One half of Happy Hardcore alongside Pierce Bleed; lost his own in-ring debut to "Swinger" Troy Grace by pinfall (an Ace Crusher counter) after nearly winning with a small package. Announced afterward that he and an absent Bleed would return the following week against a new open challenge. Delivered a comedic talent-show promo to tag partner Pierce Bleed ahead of a Gold Rush cruiserweight title opportunity, then lost a four corners contenders match on 19 May 2004 against Chris O'Brien, the One-Winged Angel, and November, driven down by a Revelator across two fallen opponents for the pin. Lost to November by pinfall on 25 August 2004 after a dropkick to the solar plexus set up the Rain Dance.

name: Tesla St. James
caption: "The Doomsayer" Kyle Lee's protege, competing in her own in-ring debut alongside Fantasy Girl and Arielle Starr in a losing effort against the Misfits.

tenures.note: Trained by "The Doomsayer" Kyle Lee, who wrapped her hands before the match; made her in-ring debut teaming with Fantasy Girl and Arielle Starr against the Misfits (Marissa Monet, Sierra Browne, and Dalbello Rage), hitting a Bastard Grinder on Dalbello Rage before Sierra Browne's Showstopper legdrop finished Fantasy Girl for the loss. Teamed with "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee in a win over Alex Extreme and a substituting Nina Grimsson by pinfall on 27 November 2004, trading holds with Grimsson before tagging out to let Lee finish the match. Teamed with "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee's own corner on 1 December 2004, cornering Alicia Powers's own opponent as Powers escaped the Red Irish for the submission win. Accompanied Kyle Lee to the ring for his own UWF World Heavyweight Championship defense against Alex Martinez on 11 December 2004.

name: Dalbello Rage
caption: The self-described heart of the Misfits, debuting alongside Marissa Monet and Sierra Browne in a win over Fantasy Girl, Tesla St. James, and Arielle Starr.

tenures.note: Introduced as the third member of the Misfits alongside Marissa Monet and Sierra Browne; made her in-ring debut in a six-woman tag win over Fantasy Girl, Tesla St. James, and Arielle Starr, absorbing a Bastard Grinder from St. James before the finish. Beat Lolita Love by pinfall (a super cradleplex) on 22 September 2004 after grinding down her legs for much of the match, then suplexed her over the top rope into sister Leanna Love's arms. Beat Angel by pinfall (a cradle-plex) on 3 November 2004 in a match egged on ringside by Sierra Browne, countering a Headhunter clothesline attempt for the finish. Played cards backstage with the Prophets of Rage on 11 December 2004, sent Marissa Monet out for muffins shortly before Monet went missing; locked the dressing room door as instructed once her brothers went looking for her. Put Marissa Monet through a pool workout ahead of her own UWF Meltdown Championship challenge to Tigress on 25 May 2005, coaching her to make the champion feel the loss of the title rather than settle for a countout or disqualification. Joined Marissa Monet in the Misfits' own backstage argument with Sierra Browne on 8 June 2005 over her handling by the promotion, then propositioned Sierra's own masseur once the room cleared. Rallied with brother Prophets of Rage members Shadoe and Derek, and Marissa Monet, against the Romanis' own interference on 6 July 2005, dubbing the alliance "Intelligent Violence," then beat "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict alongside tag partner Marissa Monet in the Misfits' own debut tag win over the Kindred (Moira Faith, Myra Benedict), earning a future UWF Women's Tag Team Championship match. Won the Women's Tag Team Championship with Marissa Monet from the Psychommunity by pinfall on 6 August 2005, then slapped the fallen Naomi Ishikawa during the celebration. Traded barbs with Nina Grimsson over Sierra Browne's own championship on 18 March 2006, then joined Marissa Monet in issuing an open Women's Tag Team title challenge.

name: Caliban
caption: Serge Annis's near-seven-foot Alaskan tag partner, debuting with a win over Fury.

tenures.note: Billed from Alaska; introduced destroying his own locker room before agreeing to team with Serge Annis against Fury (Rage and Spice), scoring the pinfall win with a superplex that drove Rage down across Annis's own outstretched knee. Teamed with Serge Annis again on 29 May 2004, billed as the Hands of Death in beating the Fraternity Boys (Chris O'Brien and Brian McKenzie) in a tag confrontation, pinning Brian McKenzie off a Near Death Experience superplex, then fighting the Ghost Dancers to a double countout in a formal tag match later the same card. Teamed with Serge Annis as the Hands of Death in a losing Gold Rush triple threat for the UWF World Tag Team Championship on 5 June 2004 against champions the Privateers and the Ghost Dancers; his own partner was taken out of the match by the Fraternity Boys' triple Conchairto before the Privateers stole the pinfall. Teamed with Serge Annis as the Hands of Death in a steel cage main event win over Kyle Lee and Alex Kidd on 28 August 2004, pinning Kidd with a Near Death Experience superplex-and-slam combination after Lee escaped the cage but could not return in time to help. His "Battle of the Sexes" match against Marissa Monet was thrown out without a decision on 18 September 2004 after tag partner Serge Annis ran in for a joint Near Death Experience; spat on the beaten Monet afterward. Lost alongside tag partner Serge Annis to Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian) by pinfall on 2 October 2004 after being distracted by a thrown frozen fish; beaten down afterward by the returning Prophets of Rage with their own tag title belts. Lost to Derek Rage by pinfall (the Hammer of God) on 20 October 2004 after an ally of Rage's, Pizzazz, jabbed a lit cigarette into his eye during a distracting brawl between Shadoe Rage and Serge Annis at ringside. Teamed with Serge Annis as the Hands of Death in a no-contest against Team Canada (Bob Jablonski, Trevor Hextall) on 13 November 2004, the match ruled a no contest after a mass brawl drew in the Sons of Cacaphony, Uriah Hawkins, Alex Martinez and Alex Extreme. Dismissed the Prophets of Rage's own history to their faces on 27 November 2004, calling Marissa Monet bait used to draw Shadoe and Derek Rage out; driven through a burning, chair-loaded table with a Flaming Godkiller by Derek Rage in the brawl that followed. A dog collar match against the Prophets was set for Rise to Power. Recalled his own past in Berwick, Nova Scotia in a vignette on 1 December 2004 before fighting the Amazing Romanis to a no-contest for the UWF North American Tag Team Championship alongside Serge Annis and hanging them by dog collars afterward. On 11 December 2004, helped Annis abduct Marissa Monet and Pizzazz, chokeslamming both off a skybox balcony onto a production table and hoisting them back up by their own chains. Arrived late, still bloodied from an earlier chair attack, to help Serge Annis beat Chris O'Brien by pinfall in a handicap match on 28 May 2005, throwing O'Brien off a balcony through a stack of tables along the way. Struck both Sons of Cacophony members with a steel chair to win a non-title four corners tag main event by disqualification alongside Serge Annis on 11 June 2005. Chained up inside the Descent Into Hell structure by Erik Grimsson on 23 July 2005, who used him to challenge the Hands of Death to defend the World Tag Team Championship in that match at Gold Rush. Pinned by Corey Irons after a chair shot on 3 August 2005; voiced a Latin battle vow via the Unitron on 6 August 2005 after partner Serge Annis's assault on Nina Grimsson and mocking of the Sons of Cacaphony.

name: Reona Yoshida
caption: A Nagoya-born wrestler who fell in a hard-fought pinfall to Angel while avenging an earlier ambush.

tenures.note: Billed from Nagoya, Aichi, Japan, weighing 137 pounds; lost to Angel by pinfall (a reverse Ace Crusher, the Headhunter) after injuring her own shoulder on a missed springboard plancha. Countrywoman Misaki Ishikawa ran in to pull Angel off a post-match submission hold. Teamed with countrywoman Misaki Ishikawa as the newly-billed Team BATTLE*DREAM in a four corners women's tag war on 25 August 2004, hooking a double DDT on Melody and Lolita Love and pinning Melody for the win; earned a UWF Women's Tag Team Championship match against the Bod Squad the following week. Lost a UWF Women's Tag Team Championship challenge alongside Misaki Ishikawa to the champions, the Bod Squad, by disqualification on 8 September 2004 after nearly finishing Brianna Landis with a spike piledriver. Teamed with Misaki Ishikawa and Sierra Browne to beat Donna Tetreault and the Bod Squad in a non-title six-woman tag on 2 October 2004, Sierra Browne's Truth Superkick finishing Brianna Landis for the pin. Co-won a women's three-way dance over Brianna Landis and Tara Smith on 20 October 2004 after she and Smith each locked on a separate submission hold on an unconscious Landis at the same moment, the referee declaring both women winners and awarding each a UWF Women's Tag Team Championship match against the Bod Squad. Lost to Brianna Landis by pinfall (a high moonsault press) on 1 December 2004 after leaving the ring to check on a blindsided Misaki Ishikawa, giving Landis the opening to finish the match. By 11 June 2005 had left the UWF for Joshi Puroresu STARDOM in Japan, ending the Team BATTLE*DREAM pairing; did not appear on the broadcast that announced it.

name: Alicia Powers
caption: Alex Kidd's wife, a member of the Powers wrestling family who surprised a tag-title-holding opponent with her own in-ring ability.

tenures.note: Married to Alex Kidd, of the wrestling Powers family; teamed with her husband to beat Tom Landis and Tara Marshall in an intergender tag match after Kidd's Somersault Bulldog set up her own pinfall. Randall Osbourne resurfaced a claim about Kidd's own past afterward, bringing out Kidd's ex-wife, Cameo, who low-blowed Kidd and hairpulled Powers to the mat. Accompanied Kidd to his own six-man tag on 15 May 2004, pulling Kari Stevens from the ring apron during the closing brawl without competing. Won her own in-ring singles debut on 19 May 2004, beating "Alluring" Arielle Starr with a Michinoku Driver after Starr's leg buckled mid-suplex. Beat Brianna Landis by pinfall (a Michinoku Driver) on 25 August 2004 after countering a suplex attempt with a European uppercut; attacked afterward by Tara Marshall and Landis until Tara Smith made the save. Teamed with Tara Smith to beat Extreme Measures (Nina Grimsson, Lisa Drake) by pinfall on 22 September 2004, hitting a Michinoku Driver on Lisa Drake before Smith's own top-rope Arizona Rattler finished the cover. Beat Tesla St. James by submission (an STF half nelson, reversed out of St. James's own Red Irish) on 1 December 2004 in her own first match back since being injured in Miami, cornered by "Tornado" Tara Smith. Beat Brianna Landis by pinfall (a 450 splash) with tag partner "Tornado" Tara Smith over the Bod Squad on 25 May 2005, pulling the win out after Landis and Marshall nearly finished her with a fireman's-carry frog splash. Accompanied husband Alex Kidd as his manager to his own double-countout match against Luke Kinsey on 11 June 2005, three days after wrestling on Meltdown. Confronted John DeWolfe alongside Lisa Drake and "Tornado" Tara Smith on 22 June 2005 over his own treatment of the women's division, recalling his past dismissal of her own wrestling ambitions. Beat "The New Blonde Bombshell" Tara Marshall by disqualification on 6 July 2005 after Brianna Landis repeatedly broke up pin attempts. Passed on Brett Greene's own invitation to Alex Kidd for a Gold Rush press event backstage on 20 July 2005, then teamed with Tara Smith as the Wind Walkers in a women's tag match against Amazing Grace and Kari Stevens that was declared a no-decision after the Bod Squad interfered. Backed debuting Samantha Daniels backstage on 3 August 2005; lost a six-person tag alongside Tara Smith and Lisa Drake to the Bod Squad and John DeWolfe by pinfall on 6 August 2005. Teamed with Brett Greene to reach the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament finals on 14 February 2006, pinned by a bridging German suplex from Leslie Hernandez; husband Alex Kidd warned Greene backstage beforehand to look after her. Teamed with husband Alex Kidd to beat Kari Stevens and "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall on 7 June 2006, escaping a Stevens dragon sleeper before finishing Stevens with a brainbuster over the top rope.

name: Scorpio
caption: A Brazilian cruiserweight, accompanied by manager and girlfriend Erika Lima, who won his UWF debut with a top-rope frog splash.

tenures.note: Billed as a Brazilian cruiserweight, accompanied by manager and girlfriend Erika Lima; beat Collision Holly in his own UWF debut by pinfall with a top-rope frog splash, the Brazilian Bomb. Lost a UWF Meltdown Championship tournament opener to Tigress by pinfall (the Poacher's Woe) on 8 September 2004, seconded by manager and girlfriend Erika Lima. Lost a UWF Meltdown Championship challenge to Tigress by submission (the Marjara Mallaka) on 17 November 2004. Lost a Road to the Gold qualifier to Vyolynce by referee stoppage on 22 June 2005, knocked unconscious by three consecutive Oblivions.

name: Kari Stevens
caption: A longtime UWF manager who forced her way onto a card and won her own in-ring debut with a corkscrew 450 splash.

tenures.note: Demanded an in-ring debut from Commissioner Becky Byers rather than continue managing from ringside; beat "Mystical" Mitzi Sukkora by pinfall with a corkscrew 450 splash in her own first UWF match. Beat Angel by pinfall in her second UWF match on 29 May 2004, reversing a hotshot attempt into a rollup for the three count, then flattening her fallen opponent with a HeadHunter after the bell. Later joined Team Canada and Tom Landis in ambushing debuting Alex Martinez in the aisle ahead of his own tag match on the same card, without competing herself. Teamed with Team Canada (Trevor Hextall, Bob Jablonski) in a losing intergender six-way against Fury (Rage, Spice) and Ami Tran by pinfall on 6 October 2004, pinned by a version of the One-Winged Angel's own Revelator from Ami Tran. Lost a UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World challenge to champion Donna Tetreault by submission (a crossface, with salt and lemon juice rubbed into a cut over her own eye) on 30 October 2004, after Trevor Hextall's own salt throw was turned back on a prepared Tetreault. Interfered for the Pride during the Bluff City Streetfight main event on 27 November 2004, supplying a snow shovel and pulling Scott Daniels clear of a top-rope elbowdrop. Tied "Hentai" Ryu Osawa in the ropes to help Trevor Hextall finish him by pinfall on 1 December 2004. On 11 December 2004, presented "Dead End" Derek Martin to the crowd as the Pride's newest member, brawled at ringside with "Supervixen" Ami Tran during Martin's own no-contest with the One-Winged Angel, and distracted the referee for Scott Daniels's own interference. Pulled the ropes from Kyle Lee's reach during his own UWF World Heavyweight Championship defense against Scott "Hotspot" Daniels on 28 May 2005, then handed Daniels the title belt after the pinfall. Lost to Ami Tran by submission (the Woman's Scorn) on 8 June 2005 despite fighting through a tweaked knee. Traded banter with tag partner Amazing Grace backstage before the two fought the Wind Walkers to a no-decision on 20 July 2005, ended by Bod Squad interference. Walked to the ring with Scott Daniels and the Pride on 23 July 2005 and introduced the Cornerstones (Daniel Kidd, Tom Landis) as the group's own new tag team. Beat Stephanie Harper by pinfall (a swinging neckbreaker) on 3 August 2005 after mentoring debuting Samantha Daniels and clashing with Arielle Starr backstage; accompanied World Champion Scott Daniels to the ring for his Brawl From The Mall 6 promo on 6 August 2005. Told a distraught Samantha Daniels backstage at Cupid's Revenge on 14 February 2006 that she did not cost her father his own Gold Rush match, laying blame instead on Alex Martinez, special referee Juan Vasquez, and UWF president Becky Byers.

Beat Pierce Bleed by pinfall with a tornado DDT on 5 May 2004, extending his own unbeaten UWF start. Swagger by pinfall on 25 August 2004 with his own standing shooting star press, the Rain Dance, after a dropkick to the solar plexus. caption: Came in at #96 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 2004, tied with four others at that placing.

tenures.note: Challenged Uriah Hawkins for the UWF Rampage Championship on 24 March 2004, losing by pinfall (a small package) after a Side Russian Legsweep left both men down. Attacked the champion from behind with a steel chair after the bell, then confronted "The Doomsayer" Kyle Lee, who ran him off; the two have an ongoing rivalry. Attacked Lee and manager Tesla St. James backstage on 15 May 2004 before Lee fought him off; the two agreed to a Gold Rush street fight. Beat "Insane Bronco" Shay Parker by pinfall on 19 May 2004 with an inverted ace crusher, promising to "make Parker famous" ahead of the Gold Rush street fight. Lost to Kyle Lee by pinfall in a Gold Rush street fight on 5 June 2004, put through a ringside table with a top-rope Gone to Texas after a prolonged weapons-filled brawl. Beat Sabbath by pinfall (The End) on 25 August 2004 after Sabbath missed a shooting star press, continuing his own vow to dismantle the UWF "piece by piece." Ambushed Alex Kidd backstage with a chair afterward before Uriah Hawkins ran him off. Substituted for a hospitalized Tom Landis and beat Alex Kidd and Uriah Hawkins by pinfall alongside Scott "Hotspot" Daniels on 18 September 2004, finishing Alex Kidd with his own End chokeslam despite Kidd having tagged out. Lost the main event to Uriah Hawkins by pinfall (an Oklahoma side roll) on 2 October 2004 after his own injured knee buckled mid-charge; turned down an on-air offer from Scott "Hotspot" Daniels to join the Pride afterward, walking away in silence. Beat Vyolynce by pinfall with a hanging brainbuster suplex on 6 October 2004. Teamed with Jamie Underwood to beat Alex Kidd and Sabbath by pinfall on 30 October 2004, Underwood countering Sabbath's own Coffin Breaker II attempt for the pin; joined Underwood in a post-match steel chair beatdown of both fallen opponents and Sabbath's wife Sayaka. Fought "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas to a no-contest on 13 November 2004 after Alex Kidd struck him from behind, sparking a brawl that also drew in the Sons of Cacaphony, Chris O'Brien and the One-Winged Angel. Was praised by Scott "Hotspot" Daniels as the "next Brett Greene" on 28 May 2005, then flattened with an inverted powerbomb (the Brett Bomb) by the returning Brett Greene himself moments after agreeing to train under him. Bonded with new Cornerstone Daniel Kidd backstage on 23 July 2005, then challenged Brett Greene to a no-disqualification rematch at Gold Rush; pinned Greene in the main event tag match after Scott Daniels turned on his own former best friend with a chair shot and a tandem finishing combination. Confronted Brett Greene and his daughter at the Eaton Centre food court on 6 August 2005, promising Greene a beating at Gold Rush before walking away without incident. Lost to debuting Juan Vasquez by pinfall (the City of Angels) on 18 March 2006 after his own Cornerstones stablemates' interference backfired.

tenures.note: Owner Edmond Winston IV's own protege, of the New Era; goaded into an impromptu match against Winston himself on 24 March 2004 after first being offered a staged loss. The bout ended without a decision when Sabbath, then Michael Augustine and Alex Extreme, then the Privateers all ran in in succession; Winston set up a handicap main event, the Youngbloods against his own New Era, for the following Rampage. Thrown from the ring early in that own handicap main event on 15 May 2004 by Michael Augustine and took no further part; pursued a legal scheme against Sabbath's custody of his own children, then beat Chad Grimsson by pinfall on 19 May 2004 with an assist from new girlfriend Sonya Benedict, who held Grimsson's leg down for the cover. Beat Sabbath by pinfall in a no-disqualification Gold Rush match on 5 June 2004 over custody of Sabbath's own children, pinning him after Sabbath's own son, Alex Price, turned on his father with a low blow and held down the cover. Won the UWF Rampage Championship from Uriah Hawkins by pinfall (a small package) on 28 August 2004, aided by a Papa Legba run-in and Ragga Bomb. Lost a UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World challenge to champion Kyle Lee by disqualification on 18 September 2004 after owner Edmond Winston IV interfered on his behalf, striking Lee with a chair and a top-rope ladder superplex. Teamed with "Dead End" Derek Martin to beat Alex Kidd and Sabbath by pinfall on 30 October 2004, countering Sabbath's own Coffin Breaker II attempt into a sitting pin; joined Martin in a post-match steel chair beatdown of both fallen opponents and Sabbath's wife Sayaka.
