Told by owner Edmond Winston IV backstage that Winston himself would face Sabbath the following week to prepare Underwood for the pay-per-view. Beat "Long Haul" Greg Embrey by pinfall (a second split-legged moonsault) on 1 December 2004 after a distracting, non-contact appearance by Sabbath and interference from Embrey's own manager. On 11 December 2004, clashed with Jessica "Fatality" Marshall backstage over her own doubts ahead of his Last Man Standing match with Sabbath, vowing to be the Last Man Standing at Rise to Power after accusing her of favoring Luke Kinsey. Was smashed through a mirror by Edmond Winston IV, then beaten down twice more by Luke Kinsey's own growing faction on 28 May 2005, including a betrayal by Scott "Hotspot" Daniels and a heel turn by Strictly Business, and was declared "exonerated from all further UWF bookings" by Kinsey. Ran in after Alex Kidd's own win over Andrew Tucker on 20 July 2005 to attack Tucker's partner Mike Sebastian at ringside. Opened the 23 July 2005 broadcast declaring independence from retired mentor Edmond Winston IV and calling out the Illuminati by name, then beat L. Dan Dee by pinfall (the Jamie Driver). Lost a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round match to Vyolynce by pinfall on 3 August 2005 after Illuminati interference; answered an in-ring challenge from Olivia Michaels on 6 August 2005, beating down L. Dan Dee until the masked wrestler pulled Olivia into the path of a chair shot and then fireballed her, unmasking afterward as the returning "Hot Stuff" Brian Von Braun.

name: Allison Ivey
caption: The Youngbloods' manager, stepping into the ring herself for the first time at Gold Rush 2004 against Angel.

tenures.note: The Youngbloods' manager, previously non-competing; made her own in-ring wrestling debut at Gold Rush 2004 against Angel, losing by pinfall (HeadHunter) after a hard-fought opening match. Attacked Angel with a chair after the bell alongside Edward Drake of the Privateers. Curbstomped Lisa Drake against the ropes on 27 November 2004 after Drake refused to rejoin the Youngbloods, then was cleared from the ring by a furious Nina Grimsson. Objected furiously in Commissioner Becky Byers's own office on 11 December 2004, first over the Youngbloods' ownership shares being staked on two upcoming matches, then over Lisa Drake being named Alex Extreme's manager against Michael Augustine. Complained to reporter Moe Owens on 6 July 2005 that the Privateers should not have to enter the Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament for a World Tag Team Championship shot already theirs by right, then worked ringside during Edward Drake's own loss to Miguel Quesada. Ran interference at ringside for the Youngbloods during Jacob Drake's own Cruiserweight Championship defense over Zero-G on 20 July 2005. Distracted the referee at ringside for Michael Augustine during his own tag team win over Miguel Quesada and Jason Keening on 23 July 2005. Discussed challenger Rick Marley's chances with the Drake brothers backstage before Jacob's Cruiserweight title defense on 6 August 2005.

name: Steve Ryott
caption: A former UWF Cruiserweight Champion who returned hoping to reform his old stable, Legion, beating Taurus in his own first match back.

tenures.note: A former UWF Cruiserweight Champion; spotted in the crowd on 21 March 2004 to on-air speculation, then announced on 29 May 2004 that he wanted to reform his old stable, Legion, with Youth Gone Wild and Alex Kidd, recruiting a bewildered Moe Owens to gather signatures. Made his own return to the ring on 25 August 2004, beating Taurus by pinfall with his own top-rope Ryott Bomb (a flying somersault legdrop) after an inverted DDT. Lost to "The Statewide Sensation" Marcus Nuit by pinfall (an inside cradle) on 6 October 2004. Lost to Luke Kinsey by pinfall (the Cherry Pop Drop) on 27 November 2004 after a competitive back-and-forth that saw both men kick out of near-falls, targeted throughout by Kinsey's own cornerman Joey. Lost to "Smooth as Silk" Miguel Quesada by pinfall (a cradle piledriver) on 25 May 2005.

name: Melody
caption: One half of a Harlequin-styled women's duo with Comedy, pinned alongside Lolita Love by Reona Yoshida's own double DDT in a losing four-way tag.

tenures.note: Teamed with Comedy in a four corners women's tag war also involving the newly-formed Team BATTLE*DREAM (Reona Yoshida and Misaki Ishikawa), the Love Sisters, and Extreme Measures (Lisa Drake and Nina Grimsson); pinned alongside Lolita Love by Yoshida's own double DDT for the loss.

name: "Hentai" Ryu Osawa
caption: A former LEW Albuquerque Champion who beat Michael Bonn in a no-disqualification Career Paths match to force the two into a UWF tag team.

tenures.note: A former LEW Albuquerque Champion and Michael Bonn's own former MBC tag partner; beat Bonn by pinfall (an underhook sit-down powerbomb, the Ecchi Trigger Finger) in a no-disqualification Career Paths match, forcing the two into a tag team under the match's own stipulation. Manager Virginia St. Ursula, who had secretly arranged the match to confront Bonn's temper, pulled a chair away from Bonn mid-match to save him from a top-rope Deadfall; Bonn attacked Osawa again after the bell before storming off. Teamed with Michael Bonn, forced into the pairing by the terms of his own prior win over Bonn, to beat the Sons of Cacaphony (Erik and Chad Grimsson) by disqualification on 16 October 2004 in the pair's own first match together, after Erik Grimsson attacked a non-competing Jacob Drake at ringside. Was beaten down by Team Canada after his own loss to Trevor Hextall on 1 December 2004, saved by a returning "Showtime" Rick Marley. On 11 December 2004, tried to stop Trevor Hextall from using a lead pipe on Spice backstage during a Pride-Fury brawl and was jumped by Bob Jablonski for his trouble. Egged tag partner Michael Bonn on through an apology to Chris O'Brien on 8 June 2005, then traded online-game banter with O'Brien once the apology was accepted. Advanced in a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005 when Niklos Romani failed to appear, accompanied to the ring by "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn and manager Virginia St. Ursula; needled tag partner Bonn beforehand over Virginia's own legs, drawing a choking grip from Bonn. Accompanied Bonn to his own Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament match on 6 July 2005 and revealed he had won naming rights to their own still-unnamed tag team. Had a football helmet placed on his own pet bird, Trice, by manager Virginia St. Ursula backstage before losing a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round match to L. Dan Dee on 20 July 2005 by pinfall (a piledriver), after Daniel Kidd ran in from the crowd and speared him into the steel steps. Escorted valet Virginia St. Ursula ringside during the Landis/Bonn match on 3 August 2005 while pet bird Trice heckled the broadcast; opened Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005 with a comic bit blaming Trice for an unpaid restaurant bathroom visit. Threw Tom Landis off the top rope during Juan Vasquez's debut match on 18 March 2006, turning back a Cornerstones interference attempt.

name: :"Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1997: #91, with no federation named beside the entry; 1998: #5, tagged SCRA, UKCW. The poll billed this wrestler more than one way across its editions: also as "Chris Douglas". Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Climbed the RSPWF Top 200 across two editions, from #91 in 1997 to #5 in 1998.

identity.note: The registry's own decorated-aka guard reads this name as a normalized substring match against the-event-dwo. Recorded distinct, not merged: the only record this entity has is a placing in the RSPWF Top 200, which gives a ring name and a federation tag and nothing else — no dates, no roster, no URL, so three of the collision doctrine's own four signals are simply absent and the no-merge default holds. Every held-promotion roster the ranked names were checked against came back with zero overlap. Reopenable the moment either side gains a record the other can be checked against.

tenures.note: Beat Taurus by submission with the End of the Show cobra clutch in his own UWF debut, seconded by bodyguard Titanicus. Fought Scott "Hotspot" Daniels to a double disqualification on 2 October 2004 under special guest referee Jason Keening, who ended the match himself and clotheslined both men from the ring after being caught between their blows. Lost a three-way dance to Scott "Hotspot" Daniels on 16 October 2004, pinned after colliding head-first with Jason Keening. Fought "Dead End" Derek Martin to a no-contest on 13 November 2004 after Jason Keening and Alex Kidd interfered, sparking a brawl that also drew in the Sons of Cacaphony, Chris O'Brien and the One-Winged Angel. His own bodyguard Titanicus lost to Jason Keening by pinfall on 27 November 2004 despite Douglas's own repeated coaching and a shove that sent Titanicus crashing into him at ringside; ambushed the victorious Keening from behind afterward with a Dragon Douglasplex. Lost a UWF Rampage Championship challenge to "Showtime" Rick Marley by pinfall (the Limelight) on 11 December 2004 after Jason Keening's own presence at the top of the aisle cost him a finish, despite a plancha and an Asai moonsault through the timekeeper's table along the way; laid the referee out with a Dragon Douglasplex afterward. Helped son Ethan de Sade ambush Jason Keening before the bell of de Sade's own UWF debut on 28 May 2005, then watched de Sade win by pinfall (the Ghostbuster). Ambushed Jason Keening with son Ethan de Sade before the bell on 11 June 2005, then beat Keening and Alex Extreme by pinfall (a schoolboy rollup by de Sade) after Extreme accidentally clotheslined his own partner. Appeared with son Ethan de Sade at his own English gymnasium on 22 June 2005, vowing alongside him to win the Road to the Gold as "the Supremacy." Eliminated first from the main event eight-man elimination match on 3 August 2005, pinned by Sabbath's Emerald Frosion.

name: "The Statewide Sensation" Marcus Nuit
caption: A nervous rookie who won his own in-ring UWF debut with a rolling savate kick into a running Lyger Bomb.

tenures.note: Signed the week before with a nervous, rambling promo previewing his own debut; won his own in-ring UWF debut over Job Holly with a rolling savate kick into a running Lyger Bomb after a flurry of quick offense, then celebrated at length with the fans. Beat Steve Ryott by pinfall with a surprise inside cradle on 6 October 2004. Talked Jessica "Fatality" Marshall by phone into a Rampage Championship shot on the Rise to Power pre-show on 1 December 2004, overheard in full by Commissioner Becky Byers. Retained the UWF Rampage Championship over "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath by pinfall (a headscissors takedown into a cradle) on 28 May 2005, surprising even himself with the counter to Sabbath's own Coffin Breaker, and declared himself "the Renegade of Rampage" beforehand. Beat Meltdown Champion Tigress by pinfall (the 51st Drop) on 22 June 2005 to become the UWF's first Unified Television Champion, unifying the Rampage and Meltdown Championships. Retained the Unified Television Championship by disqualification over "Violent" Victor Frost on 6 July 2005 after Sabbath ran in and attacked Frost, cutting a rambling promo beforehand thanking Jessica "Fatality" Marshall. Retained the Unified Television Championship over Chris O'Brien by pinfall (a Falcon Arrow) on 23 July 2005, also a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round win, after a comedic pre-match scene fretting over his own broken nose. Retained the Unified Television Championship over Tigress by pinfall (the Cradle Shock) in the Brawl From The Mall 6 main event on 6 August 2005, after a comic backstage phone call bragging about the match. Lost the Unified Television Championship to Tumaffi by pinfall (the Polynesian Burial) on 18 March 2006, after the challenger stole the title belt to rattle him mid-match.

name: Brick Rosen
caption: A power wrestler who won his own UWF tryout match against the debuting high flyer Zero-G.

tenures.note: Beat Zero-G by submission (a Boston crab) in a UWF tryout match on 20 October 2004, weathering an early flurry of high-flying offense before a botched guardrail dive left his opponent open to a powerbomb counter. Lost to L. Dan Dee by submission (a figure-four leglock) on 1 December 2004 after a game start targeting the masked luchador's own ribs.

name: Zero-G
caption: A high-flying tryout wrestler who lost his own UWF debut to Brick Rosen by submission.

tenures.note: Lost a UWF tryout match to Brick Rosen by submission (a Boston crab) in his own debut on 20 October 2004, after dazzling the crowd with a springboard armdrag and a triple jump moonsault before a guardrail-running huracanrana attempt was countered into a powerbomb. Lost to debuting L. Dan Dee on 17 November 2004 when the referee stopped the match after passing out in pain from the Figura-Cuatro Leglock, despite an early flurry of high-flying offense. Lost his own UWF debut to Tumaffi by pinfall (the Polynesian Burial) on 25 May 2005 after an early flurry of dropkicks and forearms failed to slow the bigger man down. Lost a Cruiserweight Championship of the World defense to champion Jacob Drake by pinfall (a rotating fisherman suplex) on 20 July 2005, with Youngbloods stablemates Edward Drake and Allison Ivey interfering throughout.

name: "The Bayou Badboy" Colby Greene
caption: A UWF-Eurasia wrestler who defended the UWF Eurasian Heavyweight Championship on the flagship Meltdown card for the first time, retaining in his own hometown of Baton Rouge.

tenures.note: A UWF-Eurasia roster member and billed nephew of Brett Greene, defending the UWF Eurasian Heavyweight Championship on the flagship Meltdown card for the first time in his own hometown of Baton Rouge; retained over "The Hero" Marcus Johnson by pinfall (the Bayou Bomb, a sitdown Last Ride-type powerbomb) on 20 October 2004, though the hometown crowd turned against him mid-match. Recounted his own River City Wrestling career in an interview on 18 March 2006, was confronted by Tom Landis, and fought off the Cornerstones alongside a returning Madison J. Valentine, who challenged Landis and Daniel Kidd to a tag match the following week.

name: "The Hero" Marcus Johnson
caption: A UWF-Eurasia wrestler who lost a UWF Eurasian Heavyweight Championship challenge to Colby Greene in his own first appearance on the flagship Meltdown card.

tenures.note: A UWF-Eurasia roster member, invited onto the flagship Meltdown card for the first time to challenge Colby Greene for the UWF Eurasian Heavyweight Championship on 20 October 2004; lost by pinfall (the Bayou Bomb) after a back-and-forth contest that turned the hometown Baton Rouge crowd against the champion.

identity.note: Same-named wrestlers already held in two unrelated wings; no shared roster, dates, or billing beyond the coincidence of name.

name: Bobby Nash
caption: A towering UWF-Eurasia wrestler who lost a UWF Meltdown Championship challenge to Tigress despite a large size advantage.

tenures.note: A UWF-Eurasia roster member, billed at seven feet tall; challenged Tigress for the UWF Meltdown Championship on 20 October 2004 and lost by pinfall (the Sumatran Headhunter, with the champion using the ropes for leverage) despite a large size advantage.

identity.note: A same-named wrestler already held in an unrelated 1997 wing; no shared roster, dates, or billing beyond the coincidence of name.

name: The Atomic Son Sean Malcomb
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2004: #159, tagged MBC, UWF. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Came in at #159 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 2004, tied with nine others at that placing.

tenures.note: Beat Taurus by pinfall with the Atom Smasher, a double underhook piledriver, in his own UWF debut on 20 October 2004. Lost to Vyolynce by pinfall (Oblivion) on 3 November 2004, dragging himself to the concussion-inducing finish after working over the masked man's knee for much of the match. Beat debuting "Long Haul" Greg Embrey by pinfall (the Atom Splitter) on 17 November 2004 after catching Embrey with a throat shot as he paused mid-powerbomb. Lost to Trey DaMann by pinfall (an explosive bridging dragon suplex) on 8 June 2005. Lost a Road to the Gold qualifier to "War Machine" Corey Irons by submission (the Web of Death) on 22 June 2005.
Same name and moniker, 'The Atomic Son'; an earlier run under the identical ring name, chronologically consistent with the UWF tenure this record already carries beginning October 2004.

name: "Gunman" Danny Cole
caption: A UWF tryout wrestler who helped run in on a Meltdown Championship match before losing his own first sanctioned bout to debuting Miguel Quesada.

tenures.note: Part of the six-wrestler UWF tryout group revealed to be led by a disguised T.D. Swagger, running in to help beat down "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn with an enzuiguri during a Meltdown Championship match on 3 November 2004. Lost his own first sanctioned UWF match to debuting "Smooth as Silk" Miguel Quesada by pinfall (a shooting star press) on 17 November 2004. Lost to returning "War Machine" Corey Irons by submission (the Web of Death sharpshooter) on 8 June 2005.

name: "Long Haul" Greg Embrey
caption: A veteran power wrestler, accompanied by valet Farmer Johnson's Daughter, who lost his own UWF debut to Sean Malcomb.

tenures.note: Lost his own UWF debut to "The Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb by pinfall (the Atom Splitter) on 17 November 2004, caught with a throat shot after pausing mid-powerbomb; accompanied to the ring by valet Farmer Johnson's Daughter. Lost to "Your Savior" Jamie Underwood by pinfall (a second split-legged moonsault) on 1 December 2004 after manager Farmer Johnson's own daughter distracted the referee, warned beforehand by Embrey himself to stay at ringside. Was left on the outside for the whole of Amazing Grace's own four-way singles debut match on 8 June 2005, taking a dropkick off the apron before Grace pinned Mitzi Sukkora for the win. Lost a Road to the Gold qualifier to "Money Driven" Mike Sebastian on 22 June 2005. Lost to Tumaffi by referee stoppage on 6 July 2005 after the big man ignored repeated warnings and kept striking him, then was slapped by his own valet, Farmer Johnson's Daughter, after the match. Tormented backstage on 23 July 2005 by valet "Angst" (Farmer Johnson's Daughter, revealed as Samantha Palmer), who framed his own losing streak as a debt owed to her that only "death" would settle.

name: L. Dan Dee
caption: A masked luchador, managed by Olivia Michaels, who won his own UWF debut over Zero-G by referee stoppage.

tenures.note: Won his own UWF debut over Zero-G on 17 November 2004 when the referee stopped the match after Zero-G passed out in the Figura-Cuatro Leglock; managed to the ring by Olivia Michaels. Beat Brick Rosen by submission (a figure-four leglock) on 1 December 2004 in his own second UWF outing, working over the leg throughout after his manager Olivia Michaels talked him up as a future champion. Turned heel on 28 May 2005, interrupting Luke Kinsey's own beatdown of Jamie Underwood alongside manager Olivia Michaels and joining in on Kinsey's own orders. Joined the Illuminati (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian, Corporate Leverage, Joey~!) in surrounding Alex Kidd after Luke Kinsey's own double-countout match with him on 11 June 2005, before Kinsey called the group off. Beat Youth Gone Wild in a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005, forcing him to pass out to the Figura-Quatro Leglock. Beat "Hentai" Ryu Osawa in a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round match by pinfall (a piledriver) on 20 July 2005, after Daniel Kidd ran in from the crowd to spear Osawa into the steel steps; manager Olivia Michaels accompanied him. Lost to Jamie Underwood by pinfall (the Jamie Driver) on 23 July 2005. Interfered for the Illuminati in the Underwood/Vyolynce match on 3 August 2005, pulling Jamie Underwood's leg from the floor for the pin; was beaten down alongside the Illuminati at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, then answered Jamie Underwood's own challenge by pulling manager Olivia Michaels into a chair shot and fireballing her, unmasking afterward as the returning "Hot Stuff" Brian Von Braun. Advanced in the Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament on 18 March 2006, submitting Miguel Quesada with the Von Braun Leglock after repeated attacks on his own opponent's left leg. Beat Vyolynce by pinfall, billed throughout as "Hot Stuff" Brian Von Braun, in a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament semi-final on 27 May 2006 after secretly exposing a turnbuckle, advancing to a Luck of the Draw final against Youth Gone Wild.

name: Titanicus
caption: "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas's enormous bodyguard, making his own in-ring debut and nearly upsetting Jason Keening before Douglas's own interference decided it.

tenures.note: Billed from Munich, Germany at four hundred sixty-five pounds; a former two-time APW Television Champion turned bodyguard for "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas. Lost his own UWF debut to Jason Keening by pinfall (a bridging Northern Lights suplex) on 27 November 2004 after Douglas's own ringside coaching and interference were not enough to save him. Interfered at ringside for Chris Douglas during his own UWF Rampage Championship challenge on 11 December 2004, pulling down the top rope to dump Rick Marley to the floor before being dropped by a low blow and a modified Limelight of his own. Joined Chris Douglas in a pre-match beatdown of Jason Keening ahead of Ethan de Sade's own UWF debut win by pinfall on 28 May 2005.

name: Shaun Borders
caption: A mystery returning figure who ambushed Tom Landis at ringside, shattering Landis's own crutch over his bad leg.

tenures.note: Emerged from the crowd disguised as a fan during the Bluff City Streetfight on 27 November 2004, hopping the barricade to attack Tom Landis, shattering Landis's own crutch over his injured leg before DDTing him and being hauled off by arena security; named on air but not otherwise placed in the held record. Did not appear for his own advertised 28 May 2005 rematch with Tom Landis; Landis instead beat a diminutive stand-in sent in Borders's place. Interfered in his own scheduled Road to the Gold qualifier against Trey DaMann on 22 June 2005, attacking DaMann after a look-alike stand-in, Mini-Borders, wrestled the match in his place, and was disqualified for it. Reconciled backstage with brother-in-law Rick Marley on 6 July 2005 and chose him to face Tom Landis, then lost to Trey DaMann in the companion "enemy chooses your opponent" match after apparently winning with a Diamond Dust, only for Landis to attack him and leave DaMann to score the pin. Interfered in the Landis/Bonn match on 3 August 2005, hurling Tom Landis back into a Skyscreamer and striking him with the Diamond Dust after the bell.

name: Olivia Michaels
caption: The sports agent talking up masked luchador L. Dan Dee as a future champion to anyone who will listen.

tenures.note: L. Dan Dee's own sports agent, representing him for Millenium Sports; delivered an extended pre-match speech to Brick Rosen predicting his own client's win over him on 1 December 2004, framing Dan Dee as a future UWF World Champion. Brought client L. Dan Dee to the ring during Luke Kinsey's own beatdown of Jamie Underwood on 28 May 2005, striking a partnership with Kinsey that put Dee to work whipping Underwood. Accompanied L. Dan Dee to the ring for a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005. Managed L. Dan Dee to ringside for his own Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament win over Ryu Osawa on 20 July 2005, and again for his own loss to Jamie Underwood on 23 July 2005. Was beaten down with the Illuminati at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005; threatened L. Dan Dee with termination and challenged Jamie Underwood on his behalf, only to be shoved into a chair shot and fireballed by her own charge, who unmasked as the returning "Hot Stuff" Brian Von Braun.

name: Becky Byers
caption: The UWF's own on-screen Commissioner, wielding just enough authority to unsettle even Marshall Law's own loyalists.

tenures.note: Congratulated Tigress backstage on drawing Scott "Hotspot" Daniels for the Meltdown Championship on 1 December 2004. On 11 December 2004, confiscated the Youngbloods' own ownership shares from Edward Drake, staking their return on the Privateers' own tag title defense and Michael Augustine's own match against Alex Extreme; assigned Lisa Drake as Alex Extreme's manager against Allison Ivey's own objection; and announced a UWF World Heavyweight Championship shot for Luke Kinsey against "The Last American Badass" Alex Martinez, contingent on Martinez beating Kyle Lee that same night, over Jessica Marshall's own furious protest. Denied "Violent" Victor Frost another title shot on 28 May 2005 over his own "Graphic Violence" tour conduct, booked Chris O'Brien into a handicap match against the Hands of Death as punishment for an unprovoked chair attack, and announced a sixteen-man Cruiserweight Invitational tournament with a future title shot and a fifty-thousand-dollar prize. Announced after the Meltdown Championship's own main event on 8 June 2005 that it had been the title's own last defense, with Tigress set to face Rampage Champion Marcus Nuit the following week in a match to crown a Unified Television Champion; unveiled the sixteen-man Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament's own brackets on 11 June 2005, confirmed the unification match and new title belt, announced Kyle Lee's own indefinite absence with a chronic back injury, and set a forty-man Road to the Gold Battle Royal for the following week to crown a new number-one contender for the World Heavyweight Championship. Booked John DeWolfe into a three-on-two handicap match against Lisa Drake, Alicia Powers, and "Tornado" Tara Smith on 6 July 2005 over his own role in a Meltdown brawl, needling him over stolen office supplies and a hit-and-run on her own car. Told Alex Extreme backstage on 20 July 2005, alongside Jessica Marshall, that the board of directors wanted him in a high-profile match against Jason Keening with his career on the line; separately set a Blind Stipulation Match between Donna Tetreault and Stephanie Harper for Gold Rush. Signed Samantha Daniels, Scott Daniels's own daughter, to a UWF contract backstage on 23 July 2005, after Daniels fired the Pride-appointed lawyer sent to negotiate for her. Interrupted Scott Daniels's own Brawl From The Mall 6 promo on 6 August 2005 to ban the Pride, then every wrestler, from ringside at Gold Rush and to announce a special guest referee for the main event. Denied Victor Frost a title shot and booked him for a match the following week on 18 March 2006, settled a rematch-clause dispute with John DeWolfe over a Lisa Drake grudge match by approving a Women's number-one-contender battle royal in exchange, and set a four-way World Heavyweight Championship main event for the following week between Alex Martinez, Luke Kinsey, Brett Greene, and Alex Extreme after denying both Kinsey and Scott Daniels an immediate shot.

name: "Fatality" Jessica Marshall
caption: The businesswoman behind Marshall Law itself, staking slices of her own ownership on her own hand-picked wrestlers.

tenures.note: Took a call from Marcus Nuit backstage on 1 December 2004 and, off-page, granted him a Rampage Championship shot on the Rise to Power pre-show; separately walked in on Tumaffi's own destructive studio rampage. On 11 December 2004, warned Jamie Underwood that five percent of her own ownership rode on his Last Man Standing match with Sabbath, drawing a defiant vow from him; celebrated Luke Kinsey's own win over Jason Keening as "her Hired Gun"; and was outmaneuvered by Becky Byers into a Luke Kinsey-Alex Martinez match with a UWF World Heavyweight Championship shot attached, protesting that it split her own New Era stable's own interests. Was revealed backstage on 28 May 2005 to be secretly working with Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade after brushing off an injured Jason Keening's demand for a handicap rematch, then booked Alex Extreme into an I Quit match against Keening for a UWF World Heavyweight Championship shot, upping the stakes to Extreme's own career if he lost. Told Alex Extreme backstage on 20 July 2005 that his rigged Road to the Gold pairing with Serge Annis had been her own doing, and that his only way to a title shot now was a high-stakes match against Jason Keening. Accompanied Luke Kinsey to the ring for his own match against Alex Extreme on 23 July 2005. Announced a handicap triangle match for Gold Rush pitting Jason Keening and Alex Extreme separately against Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade on 3 August 2005; appeared with the Illuminati at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005 and declared Jacob Drake and Rick Marley's Cruiserweight title defense Falls Count Anywhere. Set up Alex Extreme's brutal main-event match with Serge Annis on 18 March 2006 as a mocking "ten-year anniversary present," banned interference for the match, then urged Annis at ringside to finish Extreme off.

name: Tumaffi
caption: A self-declared "civilized savage" from the Pacific islands, wrecking the UWF's own production studio while filming his own debut vignette.

tenures.note: Introduced by an in-house vignette on 1 December 2004: took offense at a narrator's script framing him as a primitive island cannibal, smashed the UWF's own editing studio to pieces while trying to cut his own promotional video, and was billed as "coming soon to the UWF" ahead of an announced debut. Has not yet wrestled a match in the held record. Beat Zero-G by pinfall (the Polynesian Burial, a Samoan drop) on 25 May 2005 in his own first UWF match, shrugging off a flurry of dropkicks and forearms beforehand. Was warned backstage on 11 June 2005 about injuring a try-out opponent in an unscheduled dark match, mocked "Showstealer" Miguel Quesada for interjecting, then lost their singles match by disqualification after Quesada tricked the referee into believing Tumaffi had used a chair. Beat "Long Haul" Greg Embrey by referee stoppage on 6 July 2005, ignoring repeated warnings and berating the official after the bell; hid under a rolling table at ringside during Edward Drake's own Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament match against Miguel Quesada, only to be exposed and shown up by Quesada. Survived the main event eight-man elimination match on 3 August 2005 alongside Victor Frost, eliminating Jason Keening and Alex Extreme himself and splashing onto the pile that finished Papa Legba. Won the Unified Television Championship from Marcus Nuit by pinfall (the Polynesian Burial) on 18 March 2006, and had the ring announcer read out an on-air rename of the title to one of his own choosing.

name: Keith Marshall
caption: A Marshall brother who spots Brian McKenzie's bench presses and swaps beer complaints with the Fraternity Boys.

tenures.note: Spotted Brian McKenzie through a backstage weightlifting session on 1 December 2004 ahead of McKenzie's own Rampage tag match, describing himself as brother to Jessica, Tara, and Amy; sat through Chris O'Brien and McKenzie's own outrage at a new caffeinated Budweiser variant without taking a side. Carried the props for the Fraternity Boys' CareerBuilder.com routine against the Illuminati at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, then cleared the ring as the brawl broke out. Was dragged backstage into a Fraternity Boys revenge plot against Simon O'Neal at Cupid's Revenge on 14 February 2006, protesting mildly at Donna Tetreault and Chris O'Brien's escalating demands.

name: Angst
caption: "Long Haul" Greg Embrey's own valet, a wealthy owner's daughter forever accused of costing him matches by interfering.

tenures.note: Argued with her father by phone about Greg Embrey's own losing streak on 1 December 2004, then was warned off ringside interference by Embrey himself, who recalled working for her father in the AICW. Climbed onto the ring apron to distract the referee during Embrey's own loss to Jamie Underwood that night. On 11 December 2004, still pleading with her father by phone backstage over Embrey's own continued struggles. Warily paced ringside during Greg Embrey's own loss to UWF newcomer Trey DaMann on 25 May 2005, briefly considering helping Embrey up afterward. Backstage on 23 July 2005, revealed her own birth name as Samantha Palmer and began going by "Angst," framing "Long Haul" Greg Embrey's own losing streak as a debt he owed her that only "death" would settle. Confronted a triumphant Sonya Benedict backstage on 18 March 2006, needling her over family and patience before vanishing.

name: Tami Haight
caption: "Showtime" Rick Marley's own girlfriend, a wrestling reporter newly reassigned to cover the UWF itself.

tenures.note: Surprised boyfriend Rick Marley in his own locker room on 11 December 2004, freshly returned from England; revealed she had been assigned to cover the UWF for a wrestling magazine after other reporters grew wary of the promotion following the Miami incident, over Marley's own objections about her safety.

name: Pizzazz
caption: Derek Rage's own girlfriend and a Prophets of Rage regular, abducted and hung from a skybox balcony by the Hands of Death.

identity.note: An exact bare-name match against an unrelated 1997-98 federation's own "Pizzazz," a wrestler allied with a different "Rage"-named character (Medusa Rage) there; the thematic echo (a Pizzazz aligned with a Rage) is not, on its own, a two-axis join across a six-year gap and two otherwise unconnected promotions, so this is filed as a coincidental name match pending the coordinator's own review, not a merge.

tenures.note: Went missing from the Prophets of Rage's own dressing room on 11 December 2004 alongside Marissa Monet; both women were later revealed held captive by Serge Annis and Caliban in a skybox, dog collars chained around their necks, and were chokeslammed off the balcony onto a production table below, then hoisted back up by the same chains as Alex Kidd, Ryu Osawa, Paul Wong, and Stephanie Harper tried and failed to free them. Joined the Prophets of Rage's championship celebration on 18 March 2006, needling Nina Grimsson alongside Derek Rage.

name: Trey DaMann
caption: A self-declared "Undefeated Shining Star," the arrogant heir to the DaMann fortune, debuting with a win over a veteran journeyman.

tenures.note: Billed as the heir to the DaMann family fortune; beat "Long Haul" Greg Embrey by pinfall (the Trillion Dollar DDT) in his own UWF debut on 25 May 2005 after demanding an immediate world title match and being told his own opponent was a preliminary jobber instead. Declared himself the future UWF World Heavyweight Champion again on 28 May 2005, staging a lavish pre-show celebration in his own dressing room, though no title match materialized for him that night. Delivered a boastful parking-lot promo about a rival stealing his own supposed World Heavyweight Championship destiny on 8 June 2005, then beat "Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb by pinfall (an explosive bridging dragon suplex) in a preliminary singles match. Advanced in a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005 when Shaun Borders was disqualified for interfering in his own scheduled match against a look-alike stand-in, Mini-Borders; held a press conference beforehand vowing to change his pre-match routine and easily beat "John Borders." Beat Shaun Borders on 6 July 2005 in an "enemy chooses your opponent" match after Tom Landis attacked Borders with Borders's own Diamond Dust finisher and left Trey to score the pin. Beat "The Pit Monster" Chad Grimsson by pinfall (a modified Trillion Dollar DDT) on 20 July 2005 after initially trying to talk his way out of the match. Attacked Corey Irons backstage before their tag match on 3 August 2005, then fled the ring during the bout itself without taking a fall; fronted a comic CareerBuilder.com public-service segment at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005. Teamed with Amazing Grace in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, pinned by Sabbath's Vertebreaker in a pileup after refusing to plan strategy with his own partner. Mocked Brett Greene's own nephew Colby Greene on the Greene Room on 18 March 2006 and was decked and clotheslined over the top rope for his trouble.

identity.note: Two unrelated held wings carry wrestlers billed under the identical real name; no shared operator, roster, or dates link either to this wrestler's own distinct "Trey DaMann" ring persona.

name: The Mercenary
caption: Alex Extreme's longtime friend from his own UEW days, brought in as a hardcore-schooled bodyguard and enforcer.

tenures.note: Introduced on 25 May 2005 as Alex Extreme's own new bodyguard, a friend from Extreme's earliest days in the UEW locker room, brought in after an attack on Extreme's own prior second, Rodney. On 28 May 2005, warned Extreme to negotiate harder before signing an I Quit match contract against Jason Keening. Was restrained from attacking Jason Keening with his own Haliburton briefcase outside a sports bar on 11 June 2005 by a returning "Showtime" Rick Marley, then lost the UWF Rampage Championship challenge to Marcus Nuit by pinfall (a senton splash) despite using the briefcase during the match; Marley stole the briefcase during a later brawl. Beat "The First American Badass" Brian McKenzie in a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005 with a DDT after the Romanis and Rick Marley separately attacked and distracted McKenzie beforehand. Confronted Rick Marley and a returning Shaun Borders backstage on 6 July 2005 over his own stolen briefcase, then bailed Alex Extreme out of a Memphis jail cell, and struggled with Marley over the briefcase at ringside during Marley's own win over Tom Landis. Pulled Rick Marley out of a fatal four-way for the North American Heavyweight Championship on 20 July 2005 and beat him at ringside with a framed portrait taken from his own home, fleeing into the crowd afterward. Beat Paul Wong by pinfall (a second consecutive brainbuster) in the Brawl From The Mall 6 opener on 6 August 2005, sending a message to Rick Marley; later disguised himself as a store mannequin during the Cruiserweight title match and was accidentally struck with a canoe by Jacob Drake.

identity.note: Several unrelated held records carry wrestlers billed under the identical ring name "the Mercenary"; no shared operator, roster, or dates link any of them to this bodyguard, whose own backstory is tied specifically to Alex Extreme's UEW-era history.

name: Corporate Leverage
caption: A silent, suited bodyguard handed off by a departing Edmond Winston IV to Luke Kinsey, who promptly renamed him and put him to work.

tenures.note: Edmond Winston IV's own silent bodyguard, handed off to Luke Kinsey on 28 May 2005 as Winston left the UWF for good; Kinsey renamed him Ron Martin, dropped his business-suit look for a rougher one, and used him to chokeslam Jamie Underwood during a beatdown. Accompanied Luke Kinsey and Joey~! to Kinsey's own match against Alex Kidd on 11 June 2005, then joined the Illuminati in surrounding Kidd afterward before Kinsey called the group off. Cleaned house for the Illuminati against Alex Kidd and the Fraternity Boys at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, dragging a beaten Luke Kinsey to the back.

name: Joey
caption: Luke Kinsey's manservant and constant companion, along for every beatdown with a mouthful of candy and a microphone he isn't supposed to have.

tenures.note: Luke Kinsey's own constant companion, introduced on 28 May 2005 riding along in Kinsey's limousine; joined Kinsey and Corporate Leverage (renamed Ron Martin) in a five-on-one beatdown of Jamie Underwood, throwing a moonsault of his own into the assault. Accompanied Luke Kinsey and Corporate Leverage to Kinsey's own match against Alex Kidd on 11 June 2005, superkicked by Kidd at ringside, then joined the Illuminati in surrounding Kidd afterward before Kinsey called the group off. Appeared passed out during an Illuminati promo backstage on 23 July 2005, then accompanied Luke Kinsey to ringside for his own match against Alex Extreme, tapping his own wrist to signal Kinsey to leave before the count-out. Assisted the Illuminati's ringside entrance and was among those beaten down by Alex Kidd and the Fraternity Boys at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005.

name: Roxy Mayhem
caption: "Violent" Victor Frost's new valet, debuting alongside his own "Graphic Violence World Tour 2005."

tenures.note: Debuted on 28 May 2005 accompanying "Violent" Victor Frost to the ring as he launched his own "Graphic Violence World Tour 2005," jawing with ringside fans in his place. Traded barbs with Sayaka Daikin-Price alongside Victor Frost backstage on 11 June 2005, then rang the ring bell early during Frost's own match against Alex Martinez to trick him into releasing a Firebomb Chokeslam, before Frost recovered to steal the pinfall. Backed Victor Frost's own complaints about Alex Martinez's Road to the Gold win to reporter Peter Phillips on 6 July 2005, then accompanied Frost to his own Unified Television Championship match against Marcus Nuit. Visited a hospitalized Victor Frost on 20 July 2005 and was blamed by him for having been scalped bald as well, in the aftermath of Sabbath's own attack. Interfered at ringside for Frost during his own tag team win over Miguel Quesada and Jason Keening on 23 July 2005. Was warned off accompanying Victor Frost to a strip club on 3 August 2005 and rebuked when she brought up the couple's own unspoken history, left alone in a hotel bathroom as he departed for the arena. Was publicly dumped by Victor Frost on his return to UWF television on 18 March 2006.

name: Amazing Grace
caption: A brash newcomer brought in by Jessica "Fatality" Marshall to shake up the women's division.

tenures.note: Introduced on 25 May 2005 by minority owner Jessica "Fatality" Marshall as her own newest recruit from MBC, immediately running down the whole of the UWF women's division and clashing backstage with Leslie Hernandez; had not yet wrestled a match. Beat "All Night" Wendy Minow, Mitzi Sukkora, and "Long Haul" Greg Embrey in a four-way singles debut match on 8 June 2005 (a 450 splash on Sukkora for the pin), then attacked a jeering Leslie Hernandez backstage before Lisa Drake broke it up, and ran in during Hernandez and Drake's own tag match to attack Hernandez again, contributing to its no-contest finish. Traded banter with tag partner Kari Stevens backstage about the Wind Walkers before the two fought them to a no-decision in a women's tag match on 20 July 2005, ended when the Bod Squad interfered. Blindsided Arielle Starr from behind during her confrontation with Kari Stevens on 3 August 2005, setting up a Gold Rush tag match against Starr and Leslie Hernandez. Teamed with Trey DaMann in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, eliminated by Corey Irons's atomic drop after telling a reporter she needed no strategy session with her own absent partner.

name: Hellhound
caption: One half of an enhancement tag team billed as the Damned, part of the UWF's own Rising Stars newcomer pipeline.

tenures.note: Part of the enhancement tag team billed as the Damned; lost a non-title match to the Amazing Romanis by pinfall on 25 May 2005.

identity.note: An unrelated held wing carries a wrestler billed under a similar ring name; no shared operator, roster, or dates link the two.

name: Overkill
caption: One half of an enhancement tag team billed as the Damned, part of the UWF's own Rising Stars newcomer pipeline.

tenures.note: Part of the enhancement tag team billed as the Damned; lost a non-title match to the Amazing Romanis by pinfall on 25 May 2005.

identity.note: Unrelated held records carry wrestlers billed under the identical bare ring name "Overkill"; no shared operator, roster, or dates link any of them to this enhancement wrestler.

name: Moira Faith
caption: A relentlessly cheerful Japanese high flyer, billed from the Kagawa Prefecture, upsetting a returning veteran in her own UWF debut.

tenures.note: Debuted as a mystery opponent for returning "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict on 25 May 2005, winning by pinfall (a rolling Diamond Dust ace crusher) after selling a faked reconciliation hug into a suplex reversal; attacked by Benedict after the bell and busted open. Fled bloodied into the Love Sisters' own locker room on 11 June 2005 begging for help from "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict, then revealed the injury as a trick, ambushing both Love sisters alongside Benedict at the order of a man addressed as Caine. Kept Lolita Love's own kidnapped cat, Mr. Boo Boo, in a hotel room with "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict on 6 July 2005, plotting against the Love Sisters and a returning Naomi Ishikawa at Caine Tainer's own direction, then lost alongside Benedict to the Misfits (Dalbello Rage, Marissa Monet) in the Kindred's own debut tag match. Lured Lolita Love into a locker-room bathroom on 20 July 2005 and attacked her, revealing her own birth name as Akiko Masai and describing her own history with Caine Tainer and with Naomi Ishikawa, who she said had once shown her a different path; threatened Lolita with a shard of broken mirror alongside Myra Benedict and Caine Tainer. Appeared with Myra Benedict in taped footage torturing a captive Lolita Love on 3 August 2005; fought Sonya Benedict and Leanna Love to a no-contest in a handicap six-woman tag on 6 August 2005, then was knocked out with brass knuckles and dragged off by Leanna Love, who was talked out of cutting her with a katana by Lolita -- only for Lolita herself to take up the blade. Teamed with Sabbath to win the opening round of the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, struck by manager Caine Tainer backstage beforehand after trying to send him away. Teamed with "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict as the Kindred in a losing effort against "Firebird" Katie Smith and "Tornado" Tara Smith on 7 June 2006, pinned by Katie Smith's own Michinoku Driver.

identity.note: A wrestler of the identical name is separately held on another wing's own mid-2003 active roster; nothing beyond the name links the two.

name: Indigo Browne
caption: Sierra Browne's sister, filming her matches on a handheld camera at ringside.

tenures.note: Accompanied sister Sierra Browne to the ring, filming her successful UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship defense against Arielle Starr with a handheld camera on 28 May 2005; also joined Sierra in a backstage interview reminiscing about the pair's own early touring days. Reviewed tape of sister Sierra's own title defense backstage on 8 June 2005 while the Misfits argued that Sierra was being mismanaged by the promotion, defending Tigress's own mental state against Marissa Monet's mockery. Filmed sister Sierra Browne's own pre-match promo and ring entrance on 23 July 2005 with a handheld camera ahead of the Women's Heavyweight Championship defense over Angel. Tried to coax sister Sierra Browne into celebrating the Misfits' Women's Tag Team title win on 6 August 2005 and was superkicked by her for it.

identity.note: An unrelated held wing already carries a tag team of Sierra and Indigo Browne under an identical family billing; this wing's own Sierra Browne record is already on file as distinct from that wing's wrestler of the same name, and nothing beyond the shared surname links the two Indigos either.

caption: A UWF original and co-founder of the Pride, returning after years away to flatten his own praised successor with an inverted powerbomb.

tenures.note: A UWF original billed as a former World Heavyweight Champion, two-time United States Champion, Road to the Gold winner, and a co-founder of the Pride roughly a decade earlier; returned from years away on 28 May 2005 at Scott "Hotspot" Daniels's own invitation, praised "Dead End" Derek Martin as his own successor, then flattened him with an inverted powerbomb (the Brett Bomb) after Martin agreed to train under him. Invited Alex Kidd, via a message passed through Alicia Powers backstage on 20 July 2005, to join him at a Gold Rush video-game press event. Accepted Derek Martin's own Gold Rush no-disqualification challenge on 23 July 2005 by attacking him immediately, and was saved from a Pride beatdown by Alex Martinez; his own longtime friend Scott Daniels then turned on him mid-main-event with a chair shot and a tandem Pridebreaker, and Martin scored the pin. Was confronted by Derek Martin in front of his daughter at the Eaton Centre food court on 6 August 2005; hosted Alex Martinez on the Greene Room the same night, securing a promise of a future title shot if Martinez won at Gold Rush. Teamed with Alicia Powers to reach the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament finals on 14 February 2006, eliminating Alex Kidd and "Tornado" Tara Smith before falling to Alex Extreme's spinning tombstone piledriver; was warned backstage beforehand by a protective Alex Kidd to look after wife and tag partner Alicia Powers. Hosted Trey DaMann on the Greene Room on 18 March 2006, recounting nephew Colby Greene's own rise in River City Wrestling before clotheslining the young braggart over the top rope; named to a four-way World Heavyweight Championship match the following week.

name: Ethan de Sade
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1998: #33, tagged SCRA. caption: "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas's son, winning his own first UWF match after his father and bodyguard ambushed the opponent before the bell.

tenures.note: The son of "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas; beat Jason Keening by pinfall (the Ghostbuster) in his own first UWF match on 28 May 2005 after Douglas and Douglas's own bodyguard, Titanicus, ambushed Keening before the bell. Ambushed Jason Keening with father Chris Douglas before the bell on 11 June 2005, then pinned Alex Extreme with a schoolboy rollup to beat Extreme and Keening after Extreme accidentally clotheslined his own partner. Appeared with father Chris Douglas at the Douglas family gymnasium on 22 June 2005, vowing to win the Road to the Gold alongside him as "the Supremacy" and to fight through the entire UWF roster to do it. Pinned by Papa Legba with a death valley driver in a fatal four-way for the North American Heavyweight Championship on 20 July 2005, also involving Sabbath and Rick Marley. Named, with bodyguard Titanicus in tow, as Chris Douglas's own partner in a new Gold Rush handicap triangle match against Jason Keening and Alex Extreme on 3 August 2005.

tenures.source: Debuted as a touring newcomer in a Three-Way Dance on the promotion's own broadcast of 30 September 1999, billed alongside an unrelated in-story namesake (a self-described "different" "Principal" of the same surname) and boasting of past title reigns at unnamed promotions; fought the promotion's own veteran roster to a double disqualification in a card the following week, then departed the roster by the promotion's own 18 November 1999 update.

name: John DeWolfe
caption: A UWF Special Projects Division executive who interrupted a returning wrestler to dismiss the women's division, then sent the Bod Squad after her.

tenures.note: Introduced himself as a UWF head-office executive returning to television on 8 June 2005, interrupted Lisa Drake's own interview to dismiss the women's division as a sideshow, and directed the Bod Squad (Tara "Sunburst" Marshall, Brianna Landis) to ambush her after she slapped him; left ringside once Leslie Hernandez and security intervened. Brought Tara "Sunburst" Marshall and Brianna Landis to the ring on 22 June 2005 to belittle the women's division and Lisa Drake, kissing Landis on camera before Lisa Drake, Alicia Powers, and "Tornado" Tara Smith ran the trio off. Was summoned by Commissioner Becky Byers on 6 July 2005 over the resulting brawl and booked into a three-on-two handicap match against Drake, Powers, and Smith unless he could find a partner. Awkwardly propositioned Tigress backstage on 20 July 2005 about a potential Bod Squad partnership and was rebuffed after she caught him staring; managed the Bod Squad into interfering in the Wind Walkers' own tag match the same show. Told partner Brianna Landis he had gotten the Board of Directors to buy him an office air hockey table rather than get the Bod Squad out of their Brawl From The Mall match on 3 August 2005; pinned Lisa Drake for the win in that six-person tag on 6 August 2005 after Landis handed him the ring bell to strike her from behind. Negotiated a Lisa Drake rematch with Becky Byers on 18 March 2006, trading his own release-form signature for a Women's number-one-contender battle royal open to the entire roster -- which he then booked as a Bikini Battle Royal.

name: "All Night" Wendy Minow
caption: "The Rising Star," lost her own first UWF match in a four-way singles debut for Amazing Grace.

tenures.note: Billed as "the Rising Star"; lost her own UWF debut in a four-way singles match on 8 June 2005, also involving Mitzi Sukkora and "Long Haul" Greg Embrey, won by Amazing Grace's own 450 splash on Sukkora. Lost to "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson by pinfall on 6 July 2005, then shook hands with Grimsson after the match.

caption: A part-time adult performer who accompanied a returning "War Machine" Corey Irons to the ring.

tenures.note: Accompanied a returning "War Machine" Corey Irons to a parking-lot meeting with Sonya Benedict on 8 June 2005, billed as a part-time adult-film performer and old friend from Irons's own days in another promotion.

name: Virginia St. Ursula
caption: "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn's own manager, present for his backstage apology to Chris O'Brien.

tenures.note: Present as "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn's own manager for his backstage apology to Chris O'Brien on 8 June 2005, prompting Bonn through the apology and blushing at O'Brien's own joke about her. Named repeatedly across earlier UWF broadcasts as a manager to Bonn and others going back to 2003, but not previously registered under her own record. Accompanied Ryu Osawa to the ring for a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005, drawing a needling remark from Osawa about her own legs. Reassured Michael Bonn backstage on 6 July 2005 before his own Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament match, and admitted to letting Osawa win naming rights to their own still-unnamed tag team. Managed "Hentai" Ryu Osawa backstage before his own Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament loss to L. Dan Dee on 20 July 2005, putting a protective helmet on Osawa himself after he had tried to put it on his own pet bird, Trice. Escorted by Ryu Osawa to ringside during the Landis/Bonn match on 3 August 2005, calming Michael Bonn at a key moment. Managed "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn at ringside for his own UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World challenge against Luke Kinsey on 28 April 2007, leading the crowd in chants for Bonn throughout.

name: Caine Tainer
caption: A scarred, unseen figure who directs Moira Faith and "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict to attack on his order.

tenures.note: Revealed on 11 June 2005 directing Moira Faith's own faked-injury ambush of the Love Sisters alongside "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict, praising the pair's work afterward; did not appear on camera beyond a scarred face and a lit cigarette. Joined Moira Faith and Myra Benedict in cornering and threatening Lolita Love in a backstage bathroom on 20 July 2005, telling the two women they could "keep" her. Confronted Sabbath and Moira Faith backstage at Cupid's Revenge on 14 February 2006 over a photograph taken by Myra Benedict, striking Faith when she tried to send him away.

name: Mini-Borders

tenures.note: A look-alike stand-in sent out under Shaun Borders's own entrance music for a scheduled Road to the Gold qualifier against Trey DaMann on 22 June 2005; thrown around at DaMann's leisure until the real Shaun Borders arrived and broke up the pinfall, disqualifying Borders and handing DaMann the win.

identity.note: A separate performer billed to resemble Shaun Borders for a single comedic mismatch; the genuine Shaun Borders interrupts the match in person on the same broadcast.

caption: A look-alike stand-in sent out in Shaun Borders's own place for a one-off comedic mismatch against Trey DaMann.

name: "Fireball" Ken Keening

tenures.note: A retired wrestling veteran and nephew Jason Keening's own uncle; visited Jason backstage on 22 June 2005 after a mirror-smashing outburst over Alex Extreme, insisting Jason stop treating him as fragile over an old RCW attack. Revealed to Jason in a Memphis jail cell on 6 July 2005 that Extreme's own earlier attack on him had been staged with his own knowledge to provoke Jason, urging both men to see Chris Douglas, Ethan de Sade, and Jessica Marshall as the real threat.

caption: Jason Keening's retired uncle, a former wrestler who keeps trying to talk his nephew out of a self-destructive rivalry.

name: Daniel Kidd
caption: A British cruiserweight and self-described eight-years-ago Pride member, returning to the UWF alongside Tom Landis as the Cornerstones.

tenures.note: Revealed as Scorpio's mystery opponent in a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament first-round match on 20 July 2005 and pinned him with a reverse neckbreaker, then ran in from the crowd later the same show to spear "Hentai" Ryu Osawa into the steel steps, costing him his own tournament match against L. Dan Dee. Introduced formally on 23 July 2005 as one half of the Cornerstones with Tom Landis, replacing Team Canada at Scott Daniels's own side in the Pride; interfered at ringside during the main event tag match, and afterward told Derek Martin he had been a Pride member eight years earlier. Lost to Alex Martinez by disqualification on 3 August 2005 after Cornerstones partner Tom Landis interfered; he and Landis were run off by a returning Youth Gone Wild, whom Kidd then low-blowed and piledrove. Teamed with Kari Stevens in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, tipping DOOM! to the floor with a rope trick before being eliminated himself. Interfered as one of the Cornerstones during the North American Tag Team title match on 18 March 2006, then tried to blindside Juan Vasquez with a chain in his debut match before Michael Bonn tripped him.

name: Samantha Daniels
caption: Scott "Hotspot" Daniels's own eighteen-year-old daughter, newly signed to a UWF contract over her father's presumed objections.

tenures.note: Signed a UWF contract with Becky Byers on 23 July 2005 after firing the Pride-appointed lawyer sent to negotiate on her behalf, saying she meant to compete and to "salvage the Daniels name"; did not appear on camera before signing. Made her in-ring debut on 3 August 2005, losing to a returning Fantasy Girl after cornerwoman Kari Stevens's own attempted interference was thwarted by the referee. Teamed with Alex Extreme to win the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, sacrificing herself against Sabbath in the finals after being confronted backstage by a sympathetic Kari Stevens over blame for her own father's Gold Rush loss.

name: Trice
caption: "Hentai" Ryu Osawa's own pet bird, made to wear a protective helmet backstage before his tournament match.

tenures.note: Fitted with a football helmet by owner Ryu Osawa backstage before his own Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament match, over manager Virginia St. Ursula's objections; Ursula then moved the helmet onto Osawa's own head instead. Squawked from the announce position during the Landis/Bonn match on 3 August 2005; opened Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005 scolding owner Ryu Osawa over an unpaid restaurant bathroom visit.

name: DOOM!
caption: A self-declared universal conqueror in cape and mask, debuting as Lolita Love's mystery Blind Date Tournament partner after a bombastic parking-lot arrival.

tenures.note: Debuted as Lolita Love's mystery Blind Date Tournament partner on 14 February 2006 after a bombastic parking-lot arrival ranting about conquering aliens and inspiring an unrelated movie and video game; eliminated over the top rope by a Dan Kidd rope-pull trick and a Brian McKenzie knee clip, before the team advanced when partner Lolita Love finished both remaining opponents and then fell to Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie's Hart Attack clothesline.

name: Iron Eagle 3
caption: A masked debutant who mule-kicked a fallen opponent while shouting "Un Burro!" before finishing him with a 450 splash.

tenures.note: Debuted by beating Zero-G by pinfall (a 450 splash after a mule kick) on 29 March 2006. Lost to fellow debutant "The Skull Cracker" Michael Reilly by pinfall (a DDT) on 6 May 2006 after a brawl in the aisle before the bell.

name: "The Skull Cracker" Michael Reilly
caption: A hard-drinking Irish arrival who talks his way past every UWF employee he meets and has yet to lose a match doing it.

tenures.note: Debuted on 29 March 2006, arriving late and hung over but beating Taurus by pinfall (a tomikaze-style maneuver) after a brawl in the aisle before the bell. Beat fellow debutant Iron Eagle 3 by pinfall (a DDT) on 6 May 2006 after another pre-match aisle brawl, then pressed UWF President Becky Byers backstage for a title shot and was slapped for his trouble. Lost a three-way dance to debuting John Shock by pinfall (a turnaround pump splash) on 28 April 2007, having nearly missed his own introduction after being caught undressed backstage with a departing companion.

name: "Firebird" Katie Smith
caption: "Tornado" Tara Smith's younger sister, signed on the spot after outlasting a disputed bikini battle royal.

tenures.note: Signed to a contract after her own showing in a disputed bikini battle royal, then beat Fantasy Girl by pinfall (a top-rope Phoenix Splash) in her own singles debut on 6 May 2006. Came to ringside to watch older sister Tara Smith's match against Dalbello Rage the same night and brawled with Marissa Monet when it spilled outside, contributing to the match's own double disqualification. Teamed with sister Tara Smith to beat the Kindred (Moira Faith, "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict) by pinfall on 7 June 2006, finishing Moira Faith with a Michinoku Driver after absorbing a long heat segment.

name: Danny Chayne
caption: A monstrous powerhouse debutant who tore through Taurus without mercy.

tenures.note: Debuted on 6 May 2006 by beating Taurus by pinfall (the Chayne Reaction) inside a minute, having been billed beforehand as the previous week's mystery opponent who defeated Victor Frost. Lost to Madison J. Valentine by pinfall (a top-rope Air Valentine) in a battle of the newcomers on 7 June 2006, his own injured shoulder worked over throughout.

name: Brent Maverick
caption: A broad-shouldered gunslinger gimmick, one half of the Illuminati's newly-arrived Outlaws after River City Wrestling's own closure.

tenures.note: Ambushed Team Canada with tag partner Doc Holliday before their scheduled match could start on 6 May 2006, the pair's arrival billed as coming from the recently closed River City Wrestling. Introduced with Holliday as the Outlaws, the Illuminati's newest members, at a press conference on 27 May 2006, then joined Holliday in a main event loss by disqualification to Alex Extreme and Jason Keening after Team Canada interfered. Distracted the referee during Luke Kinsey's own UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World defense on 28 April 2007 while tag partner Doc Holliday tripped "Nighthawk" Michael Bonn off the top rope, costing Bonn the Hawkwind.

name: Grapes Gilmour
caption: Team Canada's veteran coach, come out of retirement to guide the duo's UWF return.

tenures.note: Introduced on 6 May 2006 as Team Canada's coach, celebrating the duo's UWF return with fans at a Baltimore sports bar before the newly-arrived Outlaws ambushed Trevor Hextall and Bob Jablonski ahead of their scheduled match.

name: Jose Lopez

tenures.note: Brought in by manager Kari Stevens on 29 March 2006 to restyle Samantha Daniels, cutting her hair and revamping her ring gear ahead of her billing as "Sweet" Sammie D that same night.

name: "The All-Around Athlete" Laura Davis

tenures.note: Confronted interviewer Moe Owens backstage, dismissing champion Sierra Browne's recent challengers -- Donna Tetreault, Tara Marshall, and Moira Faith among them -- as mediocre, and announced an open contract for the following Rampage for any woman willing to sign it. Did not wrestle.
